# What this document does

The paper reports two studies. Study 1 is the Dark Side study; Study 2 is the
Retribution study. Each has its own analysis documents, and neither is changed
here. This document sets the two studies' results side by side, computed the
same way in both, and draws the paper's figures for Study 1 and for Parts 1 to 3
of Study 2's Results.

**Reads.** Study 1's cleaned data, exactly as its own analysis wrote it; Study
2's scored data and exported tables, exactly as `01_main_analysis.Rmd` wrote
them.

**The paper's scorings (settled by the co-authors on 27 September 2026; none
is registered).** The paper scores several measures differently from the two
studies' registrations, and this document uses the paper's scorings throughout:

- **Punitiveness, in both studies, is the six components weighted equally.**
  The five attitude components (support for more punishment, two items;
  rejection of parsimony, two; three-strikes laws, two; life without parole,
  one; the death penalty, one; each the mean of its items after reverse coding)
  and the first sentence, standardized within its vignette, are each
  standardized across the sample, and punitiveness is their mean. Study 1's
  published score (`punitiveness_agg`) and Study 2's registered full index
  (`punitiveness_full`) instead averaged two halves, the eight attitude items
  and the sentence, so the single sentence counted for half.
- **Where the sentence, or anything built from it, is on the other side** of an
  analysis, punitiveness is the five attitude components, each standardized,
  then averaged; the sentence cannot be both the outcome and part of the
  score it is set against.
- **Desert theory** is the mean of Study 2's five retribution items
  (Retribution_1 to _5), and the paper's **just deserts** is the mean of desert
  theory and the proportionality principle. The registered scores keep their
  names with "(registered)".

For Study 2 the two punitiveness scores come from section 7.4 of
`01_main_analysis.Rmd` (exported per participant in `PAPER_person_scores.csv`)
and are rebuilt here from the items as a check. For Study 1 they are built here
from its cleaned data. Every Study 1 computation below is first run on Study
1's published index and checked against that study's own exports, and only then
run on the six components, so the code that produces a new number is code that
has just reproduced an old one.

**Computes.** Study 1 quantities that its own documents never exported, and a
small number of cross-study quantities. Section 3c computes every Study 1
number the paper's main text and Supplement Section S1 report on the six
components (Table 1's punitiveness column, H2 and its bootstrap interval,
Tables S1 to S3, and the statements of Section S1) and writes them to
`output/tables/` with the prefix `S1P_`. Every quantity is tied to the analysis
of record by a guard: a Study 1 number is checked against that study's exported
tables or its submitted manuscript (on the published index), or against the
independently verified values of the six-component rescoring; a Study 2 number
rebuilt here is checked against the value `01_main_analysis.Rmd` exported. The
knit stops if any guard fails. Where a guard can only check part of a quantity
(for example, a value the manuscript prints to two decimals), the comment beside
it says so.

**Writes.** The paper's grayscale figures, as PNG and PDF, to
`output/figures/two_study/`. Each paper figure's PNG is copied to the
manuscript's figure folder (`Docs/Writing/figures/paper/`), which the Word draft
embeds, and its PDF to the Overleaf project's figure folder
(`Docs/Writing/overleaf/retribution-results/figures/`). The figures are Study
1's sentences (a histogram, `fig1`) and its two correlation matrices (`fig2`,
the clusters; `fig4`, the eighteen correlates), redrawn here from Study 1's data
on the six components; the three two-study figures (`fig5` to `fig7`); Study 2's
figures for Part 2 of its Results (`fig8` to `fig13`, `fig17`, `fig18`); and
three for Part 3 (`fig14` to `fig16`). `fig3`, Study 1's sensitivity analysis on
its published index, is no longer a paper figure: it is drawn to the output
folder only. Tables go to `output/tables/`, prefixed `two_study_` (the two
studies side by side) or `S1P_` (Study 1 on the paper's scoring).

**Run order.** Knit `01_main_analysis.Rmd` first. This document reads its
exports and stops if they are missing.

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# === SETUP ===
# echo = TRUE so every computation is visible in the knitted report, as in the
# other documents in this folder. message and warning are silenced only for
# package start-up chatter. Nothing below depends on a warning being seen:
# every condition that matters is a stopifnot() guard, which halts the knit.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.align = "center")
```

# 1. Paths, packages, and a check that the inputs are the right files

```{r paths}
# === PATHS AND INPUT CHECKS ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: names every input and output, loads the packages, and
# confirms that the Study 1 data file is the one its analysis produced.
#
# PATHS ARE RELATIVE to this document's folder, so the project runs from any
# machine that keeps the two study folders side by side as they are now.
# Study 1 sits three levels up and across: Retribution/Analysis/Retribution R
# -> Punishment/ -> Punishment 2.1/Analysis/Punishment 2.1.
S1_ROOT     <- file.path("..", "..", "..", "Punishment 2.1", "Analysis",
                         "Punishment 2.1")
S1_DATA     <- file.path(S1_ROOT, "data", "cleaned",
                         "punishment_212_cleaned_data.csv")
S1_H1_TABLE <- file.path(S1_ROOT, "output", "tables", "supplementary",
                         "h1_construct_level_fdr.csv")
S1_H2_EXT   <- file.path(S1_ROOT, "output", "tables", "h2_extended_steiger.csv")
S2_TABLES   <- file.path("output", "tables")
S2_DATA     <- file.path("data", "cleaned", "retribution_scored.rds")
OUT_FIGURES <- file.path("output", "figures", "two_study")
OUT_TABLES  <- file.path("output", "tables")
# The manuscript's own figure folder. Knitting this document refreshes the
# figures the Word draft embeds, so the draft can never carry a figure that
# this analysis did not produce.
DOCS_FIG    <- file.path("..", "..", "Docs", "Writing", "figures", "study2")
dir.create(OUT_FIGURES, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(DOCS_FIG, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# The MD5 hash is a fingerprint of the file's exact contents. This is the hash
# of the cleaned file Study 1's analysis wrote, the file every Study 1 number in
# the submitted manuscript comes from. If the file has changed in any way, the
# hash changes and the knit stops, because every Study 1 value below would
# otherwise come from a different file than the published numbers did.
S1_MD5 <- "ce8752c030aaba37089bddef18f93171"
stopifnot(file.exists(S1_DATA), file.exists(S1_H1_TABLE),
          file.exists(S1_H2_EXT), file.exists(S2_DATA))
stopifnot(unname(tools::md5sum(S1_DATA)) == S1_MD5)

# Study 2's exports must exist before anything is read from them. A missing file
# means 01_main_analysis.Rmd has not been knitted since the section that writes
# it was added; knit it first.
# PAPER_H1 (section 9.19B) carries the eleven registered correlates on the
# six-component score, and PAPER_person_scores (9.19A) the paper's scores for
# every participant; both replace what this document used to read from the
# registered run on the full index (H1_correlations_full_index), which is no
# longer read here. H1_correlations (the eight-item scale) is still read, for the
# comparison of the two studies on the attitude items alone.
S2_NEEDED <- c("H1_correlations", "PAPER_H1", "PAPER_person_scores",
               "DS_personality_correlates", "DS_revenge_darkside",
               "DS_cluster_correlations", "DS_tautology_ladder",
               "DS_H2_by_part", "H2_steiger", "E2_solidarity_steiger",
               "descriptives", "sentence_ceiling_share", "sentence_modal_share")
S2_MISSING <- S2_NEEDED[!file.exists(file.path(S2_TABLES,
                                               paste0(S2_NEEDED, ".csv")))]
if (length(S2_MISSING)) stop("Knit 01_main_analysis.Rmd first. Missing: ",
                             paste(S2_MISSING, collapse = ", "))

library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)   # stacks two panels into one figure
# Section 3c also uses boot (the bootstrap), car (type 3 tests), lme4 (the
# mixed model) and psych (Cronbach's alpha). Each is called with its package
# name (boot::boot(), car::Anova() and so on) rather than attached, so none of
# them can mask a function this document uses under the same name.
stopifnot(requireNamespace("boot", quietly = TRUE),
          requireNamespace("car", quietly = TRUE),
          requireNamespace("lme4", quietly = TRUE),
          requireNamespace("psych", quietly = TRUE))

s1 <- read.csv(S1_DATA, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
s2 <- as.data.frame(readRDS(S2_DATA))
read_s2 <- function(name) read.csv(file.path(S2_TABLES, paste0(name, ".csv")),
                                   stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
stopifnot(nrow(s1) == 496, nrow(s2) == 948)
cat(sprintf("Study 1: %d participants. Study 2: %d participants.\n",

```

# 2. One comparison function, checked against the analysis of record

```{r steiger}
# === THE DEPENDENT-CORRELATION COMPARISON ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: defines the one function every comparison between two
# correlations goes through below, then proves it computes exactly what the main
# analysis computes before it is used for anything.
#
# THE TEST. Two correlations measured on the same people share those people, so
# their difference cannot be tested as if they came from two samples. Steiger's
# (1980) test handles that dependence; Zou's (2007) interval gives the range of
# differences the data leave standing. Both come from cocor, the package
# 01_main_analysis.Rmd uses, called the same way. j is the variable the two
# correlations share (punitiveness); k and h are the two rivals.
# THE p IS ONE-SIDED ("greater": k correlates more strongly than h), as in the
# registered tests. Study 1's manuscript reports two-sided p values, so the
# column is named p_one_sided and a two-sided p is added beside it.
two_steiger <- function(data, j, k, h) {
  ok <- stats::complete.cases(data[[j]], data[[k]], data[[h]])
  x  <- data[ok, ]
  r_jk <- cor(x[[j]], x[[k]]); r_jh <- cor(x[[j]], x[[h]])
  r_kh <- cor(x[[k]], x[[h]]); n <- nrow(x)
  res <- cocor::cocor.dep.groups.overlap(
    r.jk = r_jk, r.jh = r_jh, r.kh = r_kh, n = n,
    alternative = "greater", test = c("steiger1980", "zou2007"),
    return.htest = TRUE)
  z <- unname(res$steiger1980$statistic)
  data.frame(r_jk = r_jk, r_jh = r_jh, r_kh = r_kh, n = n, diff = r_jk - r_jh,
             diff_lower = res$zou2007$conf.int[1],
             diff_upper = res$zou2007$conf.int[2],
             z = z, p_one_sided = res$steiger1980$p.value,
             p_two_sided = 2 * pnorm(-abs(z)))
}

# GUARD 1. The registered H2 exactly as 01_main_analysis.Rmd exported it: both
# correlations, the difference, both ends of its interval, and z. (Its p
# underflows to zero, so the p is checked on the next guard instead.)
g2 <- two_steiger(s2, "punitiveness", "hostile_agg", "crime_concerns")
h2_rec <- read_s2("H2_steiger")
for (f in c("r_jk", "r_jh", "diff", "diff_lower", "diff_upper", "z"))
  stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(g2[[f]], h2_rec[[f]], tolerance = 1e-8)))
# GUARD 2. The E2 comparison, whose p is small but not zero, so the p the
# function returns is checked as well.
ge2 <- two_steiger(s2, "punitiveness", "solidarity_hostile", "solidarity_durk")
e2_rec <- read_s2("E2_solidarity_steiger")
for (f in c("diff", "diff_lower", "diff_upper", "z"))
  stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(ge2[[f]], e2_rec[[f]], tolerance = 1e-8)))
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(ge2$p_one_sided, e2_rec$p, tolerance = 1e-8)))
cat("The comparison function reproduces Study 2's H2 and E2 exactly.\n")
```

# 3. Study 1, computed from its cleaned data and checked against its record

```{r study1_scores}
# === 3.0 STUDY 1'S PUNITIVENESS: THE PUBLISHED INDEX AND THE PAPER'S TWO SCORES ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: adds the paper's two punitiveness scores to s1, built
# exactly as Study 2's section 7.4 builds them, after checking that Study 1's
# published score is what this document takes it to be.
#   s1$punit_six     SIX COMPONENTS WEIGHTED EQUALLY, the paper's punitiveness
#                    in the main text: the five attitude components and the
#                    first sentence (Sentence_z, standardized within vignette),
#                    each standardized across the sample, then averaged.
#   s1$punit_five_z  THE FIVE ATTITUDE COMPONENTS, EACH STANDARDIZED, averaged:
#                    the paper's punitiveness wherever the sentence is on the
#                    other side of an analysis. In Study 1 that is only Table
#                    S3, whose outcome is the sentence.
# PREREG: NOT REGISTERED. Study 1's registered and published primary measure is
#         punitiveness_agg, the eight-item scale and the sentence each
#         standardized and averaged, so that the one sentencing decision counts
#         for half of the score. The co-authors decided on 27 September 2026
#         that the sentence is one component of six, not half. punitiveness_agg
#         is kept in s1, unchanged: every Study 1 guard below reproduces the
#         published numbers on it before the same code is run on punit_six.
# CONSUMES: s1 (section 1).
# DANGER: never overwrite s1$punitiveness_agg with a new score. The guards in
#         sections 3, 3b and 3c check this document's code against Study 1's
#         exports through that column; if it changed, those guards would check
#         the new score against the old exports and stop the knit, or worse,
#         be edited to pass.

# zmean(): standardize each argument across the sample, then average them for
# each participant. It is a copy of the helper in 01_main_analysis.Rmd (section
# 0.3), which builds Study 2's six-component score with it, so both studies'
# scores come from the same rule. Standardizing first is what makes the parts
# count equally: the attitude components are 1-to-7 means with different
# spreads and the sentence is already a z-score, so a plain mean would let the
# widest-spread part count for most.
zmean <- function(...) {
  m <- scale(cbind(...))
  out <- rowMeans(m, na.rm = TRUE)
  out[is.nan(out)] <- NA_real_
  as.numeric(out)
}

# --- The components, as Study 1's cleaned file stores them -------------------
# Study 1's cleaning built each two-item component as the mean of its items
# after reverse coding (the _R columns), and the one-item components are the
# items themselves. GUARD: every component is exactly that mean, so the six
# components here are the ones the published scale was built from, and no
# participant is missing any of them (Study 1 required every answer).
S1_ITEMS8 <- c("punishmore_1_R", "punishmore_2", "parsimony_1_R", "parsimony_2_R",
               "threestrikes_1", "threestrikes_2", "LWOP", "deathpenalty")
S1_PARTS  <- c("punishmore_comp", "parsimony_comp", "threestrikes_comp",
               "LWOP", "deathpenalty")
stopifnot(!anyNA(s1[, c(S1_ITEMS8, S1_PARTS, "Sentence_z", "Sentence_1")]),
          max(abs(s1$punishmore_comp -
                    rowMeans(s1[, c("punishmore_1_R", "punishmore_2")]))) < 1e-12,
          max(abs(s1$parsimony_comp -
                    rowMeans(s1[, c("parsimony_1_R", "parsimony_2_R")]))) < 1e-12,
          max(abs(s1$threestrikes_comp -
                    rowMeans(s1[, c("threestrikes_1", "threestrikes_2")]))) < 1e-12)

# --- The published index, rebuilt ------------------------------------------
# GUARD: Study 1's sentence z-score is the first sentence standardized within
# each vignette, and its published index is the mean of the standardized
# eight-item scale and that z-score. Rebuilt from the items, both agree with
# the stored columns to rounding error. This pins down what "the published
# index" means in every comparison below.
s1_sz <- ave(s1$Sentence_1, s1$vignette, FUN = function(x) as.numeric(scale(x)))
s1_old_rebuilt <- rowMeans(cbind(as.numeric(scale(rowMeans(s1[, S1_ITEMS8]))),
                                 s1$Sentence_z))
stopifnot(max(abs(s1_sz - s1$Sentence_z)) < 1e-10,
          max(abs(s1_old_rebuilt - s1$punitiveness_agg)) < 1e-10,
          max(abs(rowMeans(s1[, S1_ITEMS8]) - s1$punitiveness_8item)) < 1e-10)

# --- The paper's two scores --------------------------------------------------
s1$punit_six <- zmean(s1$punishmore_comp, s1$parsimony_comp, s1$threestrikes_comp,
                      s1$LWOP, s1$deathpenalty, s1$Sentence_z)
s1$punit_five_z <- zmean(s1$punishmore_comp, s1$parsimony_comp,
                         s1$threestrikes_comp, s1$LWOP, s1$deathpenalty)
# GUARDS, against the independently verified rescoring of Study 1 (scratch
# report "study1-six", 27 Sep 2026): the six-component score correlates .928
# with the published index and .967 with the eight-item scale, and the
# standardized five-component score correlates .99 with the eight-item scale
# (it is the eight attitude items reweighted so each component counts a fifth;
# a component turned upside down would pull this far lower).
stopifnot(!anyNA(s1$punit_six), !anyNA(s1$punit_five_z),
          round(cor(s1$punit_six, s1$punitiveness_agg), 3) == 0.928,
          round(cor(s1$punit_six, s1$punitiveness_8item), 3) == 0.967,
          round(cor(s1$punit_five_z, s1$punitiveness_8item), 2) == 0.99)
cat(sprintf(paste("Study 1: six components vs the published index r = %.3f;",
                  "vs the eight-item scale r = %.3f;",
                  "five components vs the eight-item scale r = %.3f.\n"),
            cor(s1$punit_six, s1$punitiveness_agg),
            cor(s1$punit_six, s1$punitiveness_8item),
            cor(s1$punit_five_z, s1$punitiveness_8item)))
```

```{r study1}
# === STUDY 1 QUANTITIES ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: computes, from Study 1's cleaned data, every Study 1
# number the two-study comparisons need, on the paper's punitiveness score.
# PUNITIVENESS is the six components weighted equally (s1$punit_six, section
# 3.0), in both studies (Study 2's matching score is 01's punit_parts6, read in
# section 4). NOT REGISTERED: see section 3.0.
# HOW EACH NUMBER IS CHECKED: each computation is first run on Study 1's
# published index (punitiveness_agg) and checked against Study 1's exported
# tables or its submitted manuscript; the identical code is then run on
# punit_six, and those are the numbers this document uses. The published-index
# versions carry the suffix _old and are used for nothing but the guards.
# CONSUMES: s1 with punit_six (3.0), two_steiger() (section 2).

# --- A. The sixteen constructs both studies fielded -------------------------
# Construct columns as Study 1 named them, paired with the one label each
# carries in every table and figure of the paper, in Study 1's order. Revenge is
# Study 1's three-item scale; Study 2's matching column is its three-item scoring
# of the same items, not its registered four.
s1_constructs <- c(
  harsh_comp       = "Harsh prison conditions",
  exclusion_comp   = "Social exclusion",
  hatred_comp      = "Hatred",
  suffering_comp   = "Infliction of suffering",
  rwa_comp         = "Right-wing authoritarianism",
  raceresent_comp  = "Racial resentment",
  anger_comp       = "Anger",
  degradation_comp = "Degradation",
  dueprocess_comp  = "Due-process permissiveness",
  revenge_comp     = "Revenge (three shared items)",
  vprone_comp      = "Violence proneness",
  crime_rates_comp = "Perceived crime rates",
  uncertain_comp   = "Convicting on uncertain evidence",
  prisonvi_comp    = "Tolerance of prison violence",
  sdo_comp         = "Social dominance orientation",
  fear_comp        = "Fear of crime")
# Fisher-z 95% interval, the same interval cor.test() and the main analysis use.
cor_ci <- function(x, y) {
  tt <- cor.test(x, y)
  data.frame(r = unname(tt$estimate), ci_lower = tt$conf.int[1],
             ci_upper = tt$conf.int[2], n = sum(complete.cases(x, y)))
}
con_table <- function(score) do.call(rbind, lapply(names(s1_constructs), function(v)
  cbind(construct = unname(s1_constructs[v]), cor_ci(s1[[score]], s1[[v]]))))
# GUARD: on the published index, every correlation against Study 1's own
# exported H1 table, to the three decimals that table prints.
s1_con_old <- con_table("punitiveness_agg")
s1_h1 <- read.csv(S1_H1_TABLE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
s1_h1_r <- setNames(s1_h1$r, s1_h1$Construct)[names(s1_constructs)]
stopifnot(!anyNA(s1_h1_r), all(abs(round(s1_con_old$r, 3) - s1_h1_r) < 1e-9))
# The paper's numbers: the same sixteen correlations on the six components.
s1_con <- con_table("punit_six")

# --- B. The four clusters ---------------------------------------------------
s1_clusters <- c(hostile_agg        = "Hostile aggression",
                 emotions_agg       = "Emotions",
                 personality_agg    = "Personality and ideology",
                 crime_concerns_agg = "Crime concerns")
clu_table <- function(score) do.call(rbind, lapply(names(s1_clusters), function(v)
  cbind(cluster = unname(s1_clusters[v]), cor_ci(s1[[score]], s1[[v]]))))
# GUARD: on the published index, against Study 1's exported cluster table, to
# its three decimals.
s1_clu_old <- clu_table("punitiveness_agg")
s1_h2x <- read.csv(S1_H2_EXT, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
stopifnot(all(abs(round(s1_clu_old$r[1:3], 3) - s1_h2x$r_Cluster[1:3]) < 1e-9),
          abs(round(s1_clu_old$r[4], 3) - s1_h2x$r_Crime[1]) < 1e-9)
# The paper's numbers. GUARD: the verified six-component values (hostile
# aggression .690, emotions .622, personality .597, crime concerns .360).
s1_clu <- clu_table("punit_six")
stopifnot(all(abs(round(s1_clu$r, 3) - c(.690, .622, .597, .360)) < 1e-9))
# Study 1's personality cluster pools thirty items, including trait
# vengefulness and blood sports viewership, which Study 2 did not field. For a
# like-for-like comparison, the cluster is also rebuilt here from the twenty-one
# items of the four measures both studies share. The figure shows the published
# thirty-item value; this one is reported beside it.
shared_personality_items <- c("rwa_1", "rwa_2", "rwa_3_R", "rwa_4", "rwa_5",
                              "sdo_1", "sdo_2", "sdo_3_R", "sdo_4_R", "sdo_5",
                              "sdo_6", "sdo_7_R", "sdo_8_R",
                              paste0("vprone_", 1:4),
                              "Raceresent_1_R", "Raceresent_2", "Raceresent_3",
                              "Raceresent_4_R")
stopifnot(all(shared_personality_items %in% names(s1)))
s1$personality_shared <- rowMeans(s1[, shared_personality_items], na.rm = TRUE)
s1_pers_shared <- cor_ci(s1$punit_six, s1$personality_shared)
# GUARD: the verified six-component value, .629 (the published index gave .513).
stopifnot(round(s1_pers_shared$r, 3) == 0.629,
          round(cor(s1$punitiveness_agg, s1$personality_shared), 3) == 0.513)

# --- C. The three-level sensitivity analysis -------------------------------
# Study 1's own levels (03_supplementary_analyses.Rmd): all six hostility
# constructs; four, with suffering and harsh conditions dropped; exclusion and
# revenge alone. The two narrower levels average composites, as that study
# built them.
s1$hostile_cons   <- rowMeans(s1[, c("exclusion_comp", "degradation_comp",
                                     "prisonvi_comp", "revenge_comp")],
                              na.rm = TRUE)
s1$hostile_strict <- rowMeans(s1[, c("exclusion_comp", "revenge_comp")],
                              na.rm = TRUE)
LEVELS <- c("All six constructs", "Four constructs", "Exclusion and revenge only")
ladder_table <- function(score) {
  out <- do.call(rbind, list(
    two_steiger(s1, score, "hostile_agg",    "crime_concerns_agg"),
    two_steiger(s1, score, "hostile_cons",   "crime_concerns_agg"),
    two_steiger(s1, score, "hostile_strict", "crime_concerns_agg")))
  out$row <- LEVELS
  out
}
# GUARD: on the published index, the manuscript prints these three differences
# to three decimals and their Steiger Zs to two.
s1_ladder_old <- ladder_table("punitiveness_agg")
stopifnot(all(abs(s1_ladder_old$diff - c(.264, .226, .221)) < .0005),
          all(abs(s1_ladder_old$z - c(6.26, 5.07, 5.05)) < .005))
# The paper's numbers. GUARD: the verified six-component differences (.331,
# .286, .263) and Zs (8.54, 6.90, 6.38).
s1_ladder <- ladder_table("punit_six")
stopifnot(all(abs(round(s1_ladder$diff, 3) - c(.331, .286, .263)) < 1e-9),
          all(abs(round(s1_ladder$z, 2) - c(8.54, 6.90, 6.38)) < 1e-9))

# --- D. Each component of punitiveness separately --------------------------
# In the order the manuscript reports them, which is also the order of the
# figure panel and of the text. Each part is tested on its own, so how the
# parts are weighted into one score does not enter here: these rows are the
# same under the published index and the six components.
PARTS <- c(punishmore_comp   = "Punish more",
           parsimony_comp    = "Rejection of parsimony",
           deathpenalty      = "Death penalty",
           threestrikes_comp = "Three strikes",
           LWOP              = "Life without parole",
           Sentence_z        = "The sentencing decision")
s1_bypart <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(PARTS), function(v)
  two_steiger(s1, v, "hostile_agg", "crime_concerns_agg")))
s1_bypart$row <- unname(PARTS)
# GUARD: the manuscript prints these differences to TWO decimals (.34, .31,
# .32, .22, .15, .08) and the Zs to two. The differences are therefore checked
# at the precision the manuscript prints; the Zs pin the computation down more
# tightly. The sentence is Sentence_z, the within-vignette z-score, which gives
# Z = 1.60 (the raw years would give 1.59).
stopifnot(all(abs(round(s1_bypart$diff, 2) - c(.34, .31, .32, .22, .15, .08)) < 1e-9),
          all(abs(s1_bypart$z - c(8.23, 6.70, 7.23, 5.06, 3.27, 1.60)) < .005))

# --- E. The twelve shared constructs on the eight-item scale ---------------
# Study 1's eight attitude items, without the sentence, against the same twelve
# constructs Study 2 registered (revenge on the three shared items). Set beside
# Study 2's eight-item correlations, this shows whether the two studies differ on
# the attitude items themselves or only once the sentence is folded in.
s1_eight <- do.call(rbind, lapply(setdiff(names(s1_constructs),
                                          c("rwa_comp", "raceresent_comp",
                                            "vprone_comp", "sdo_comp")),
  function(v) cbind(construct = unname(s1_constructs[v]),
                    cor_ci(s1$punitiveness_8item, s1[[v]]))))
cat("Study 1: on the published index, all sixteen constructs, the four clusters,\n")
cat("the three levels of the sensitivity analysis and all six parts reproduce\n")
cat("Study 1's record; the same code on the six components gives the paper's values.\n")
```

# 3b. Study 1 descriptives that the Method and the Supplement report

```{r study1_reported}
# === STUDY 1 NUMBERS REPORTED IN THE METHOD AND THE SUPPLEMENT ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: computes four Study 1 descriptives that the paper
# reports but that no Study 1 output prints, and writes them, one row each,
# to output/tables/two_study_s1_descriptives.csv. Each is checked against the
# Study 1 export it can be checked against. None involves a punitiveness score.
#   1. The shares of liberals, moderates and conservatives (the Method).
#   2. The median completion time and its interquartile range (the Method).
#   3. The first and last day a response was started (the Method).
#   4. Sentences compared across the three political groups by a one-way
#      analysis of variance (Supplement, Section S1). Not preregistered.
# MOVED: the median range of each correlate's correlation with punitiveness
# across the three vignettes used to be a fifth row here, on the published
# index. It now depends on the punitiveness score, so it is computed in section
# 3c on the six components (with the published-index value reproduced as a
# guard) and written to S1P_vignette_summary.csv; this file no longer has it.
# CONSUMES: s1 and S1_ROOT (section 1).
# NOTHING HERE CHANGES s1 OR ANY NUMBER ABOVE.

s1_out <- list()
add_s1 <- function(quantity, value, detail) {
  s1_out[[length(s1_out) + 1]] <<- data.frame(quantity = quantity, value = value,
                                                detail = detail,
                                                stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

# --- 1. Political groups ------------------------------------------------------
# Study 1 groups the 1-7 liberal-conservative item as 1 to 3 = liberal, 4 =
# moderate, 5 to 7 = conservative (its 01_main_analysis.Rmd, "Recode political
# orientation"). GUARD: the column in the cleaned file follows that rule for
# every participant, and the group sizes match Study 1's exported table of
# sentences by political group.
s1_pol <- read.csv(file.path(S1_ROOT, "output", "tables", "supplementary",
                             "sentence_anchor_by_political_group.csv"),
                   stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
rule <- ifelse(s1$politid <= 3, "Liberal", ifelse(s1$politid == 4, "Moderate",
                                                  "Conservative"))
stopifnot(identical(rule, s1$political_group), !anyNA(s1$political_group))
pol_n <- table(factor(s1$political_group,
                      levels = c("Liberal", "Moderate", "Conservative")))
stopifnot(all(pol_n[s1_pol$political_group] == s1_pol$n))
for (g in names(pol_n))
  add_s1(paste("percent", tolower(g)), 100 * unname(pol_n[g]) / nrow(s1),
         sprintf("%d of %d", unname(pol_n[g]), nrow(s1)))

# --- 2. Completion time -------------------------------------------------------
# Qualtrics records the time from opening the survey to submitting it, in
# seconds. Quartiles use R's default quantile rule (type 7).
mins <- s1$Duration..in.seconds. / 60
stopifnot(!anyNA(mins), length(mins) == 496)
q <- stats::quantile(mins, c(.25, .50, .75))
add_s1("completion minutes, median", unname(q[2]), "")
add_s1("completion minutes, 25th percentile", unname(q[1]), "")
add_s1("completion minutes, 75th percentile", unname(q[3]), "")

# --- 3. Dates of collection ---------------------------------------------------
# The cleaned file has no start date, so the dates come from the last raw
# Qualtrics export, matched on ResponseId. A Qualtrics export has two further
# header rows (question text and import ids) under the column names, which are
# dropped. Only two columns are kept; the file's IP address and location
# columns are never read into anything that is written out.
S1_RAW <- file.path("..", "..", "..", "Punishment 2.1", "Data",
                    "PUNISHMENT 2.1 -  Pro-Social_January 7, 2026_20.47.csv")
raw <- read.csv(S1_RAW, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
raw <- raw[-(1:2), c("ResponseId", "StartDate")]
# GUARD: every analyzed participant is in this export, once.
stopifnot(all(s1$ResponseId %in% raw$ResponseId), !anyDuplicated(raw$ResponseId))
started <- as.Date(substr(raw$StartDate[match(s1$ResponseId, raw$ResponseId)], 1, 10))
stopifnot(!anyNA(started))
add_s1("first start date", NA_real_, format(min(started)))
add_s1("last start date", NA_real_, format(max(started)))

# --- 4. Sentences across the three political groups ---------------------------
# GUARD: the group means match Study 1's exported table before the test is run.
pol_means <- tapply(s1$Sentence_1, s1$political_group, mean)
stopifnot(all(abs(round(pol_means[s1_pol$political_group], 2) - s1_pol$mean_sent) < 1e-9))
pol_aov <- stats::anova(stats::lm(Sentence_1 ~ political_group, data = s1))
add_s1("sentence by political group, F", pol_aov[1, "F value"],
       sprintf("df = %d, %d; p = %.4f", pol_aov[1, "Df"], pol_aov[2, "Df"],
               pol_aov[1, "Pr(>F)"]))

# (The former item 5, the stability of the correlations across vignettes, is
# in section 3c; see MOVED in the header of this chunk.)

s1_reported <- do.call(rbind, s1_out)
write.csv(s1_reported, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "two_study_s1_descriptives.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
print(s1_reported, row.names = FALSE, digits = 4)
```

# 3c. Study 1 on the paper's scoring: Table 1, H2, and Supplement Section S1

The paper reports Study 1 with punitiveness scored as six components weighted
equally (section 3.0). Study 1's own documents computed every number on its
published index, so this section recomputes, from Study 1's cleaned data, each
Study 1 number the paper's main text and Supplement Section S1 report that
involves a punitiveness score:

- Table 1's last column (the eighteen correlates and five clusters) and its
  punitiveness row (number of parts, reliability, mean, SD);
- H2 (hostile aggression against crime concerns) with its bootstrap interval,
  the other clusters against crime concerns, the three levels of strictness
  (Table S1), and the check without the parsimony items;
- the demographic moderation tests (Tables S2 and S3);
- Section S1's statements about punitiveness by political group, gender, race,
  age and education, and about the stability of the correlations across the
  three vignettes.

**How each number is checked.** Every computation is run twice with the same
code: first on the published index, where the result must reproduce Study 1's
own export (the knit stops if it does not), then on the six components. The
six-component results are checked against the independently verified values of
the rescoring (scratch reports "study1-six", 27 September 2026). Only the
six-component results are written, to `output/tables/S1P_*.csv`. None of this is
registered: Study 1's registration and its published analyses used the index.

```{r s1p_setup}
# === 3c.0 SHARED PIECES FOR THE STUDY 1 RESCORING ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: checks that the Study 1 exports the guards below compare
# against exist, and defines the two helpers every chunk in 3c uses.
# PREREG: NOT REGISTERED (the paper's scoring; see section 3.0).
# CONSUMES: S1_ROOT, OUT_TABLES (section 1); s1 with punit_six and punit_five_z
#           (section 3.0).

# Study 1's own exports, each written by its 01_main_analysis.Rmd or
# 03_supplementary_analyses.Rmd. They are read only to check that the code here
# reproduces the published numbers before it computes new ones.
S1_SUPP <- file.path(S1_ROOT, "output", "tables", "supplementary")
S1P_REFERENCE <- c(
  file.path(S1_ROOT, "output", "tables", "reliability_alphas.csv"),
  file.path(S1_ROOT, "output", "tables", "h2_extended_steiger.csv"),
  file.path(S1_ROOT, "output", "tables", "vignette_correlation_stability.csv"),
  file.path(S1_SUPP, "h1_construct_level_fdr.csv"),
  file.path(S1_SUPP, "tautology_steiger_by_level.csv"),
  file.path(S1_SUPP, "tautology_bootstrap_cis.csv"),
  file.path(S1_SUPP, "parsimony_sensitivity.csv"),
  file.path(S1_SUPP, "interactions_punitiveness_agg.csv"),
  file.path(S1_SUPP, "interactions_sentence_z.csv"),
  file.path(S1_SUPP, "punitiveness_levels_by_demographic.csv"),
  file.path(S1_SUPP, "punitiveness_means_political.csv"))
stopifnot(all(file.exists(S1P_REFERENCE)))
read_s1 <- function(path) read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# s1p_write(): writes one S1P_ table to output/tables and remembers its name, so
# the chunk at the end of 3c can list everything this section wrote.
S1P_WRITTEN <- character(0)
s1p_write <- function(df, name) {
  write.csv(df, file.path(OUT_TABLES, paste0("S1P_", name, ".csv")), row.names = FALSE)
  S1P_WRITTEN <<- c(S1P_WRITTEN, paste0("S1P_", name))
  invisible(df)
}

# s1p_steiger(): Steiger's (1980) test of two correlations that share one
# variable (j, the punitiveness score), TWO-SIDED, exactly as Study 1's
# run_steiger() calls cocor (its default alternative), plus Zou's (2007) 95%
# interval for the difference. Section 2's two_steiger() runs the registered
# one-sided test for Study 2; Study 1's manuscript reports two-sided p values,
# so this section uses its own call rather than converting.
s1p_steiger <- function(data, j, k, h) {
  r_jk <- cor(data[[j]], data[[k]]); r_jh <- cor(data[[j]], data[[h]])
  r_kh <- cor(data[[k]], data[[h]]); n <- nrow(data)
  res <- cocor::cocor.dep.groups.overlap(
    r.jk = r_jk, r.jh = r_jh, r.kh = r_kh, n = n,
    test = c("steiger1980", "zou2007"), return.htest = TRUE)
  data.frame(r_jk = r_jk, r_jh = r_jh, r_kh = r_kh, n = n, diff = r_jk - r_jh,
             diff_lower = res$zou2007$conf.int[1],
             diff_upper = res$zou2007$conf.int[2],
             z = unname(res$steiger1980$statistic),
             p_two = res$steiger1980$p.value)
}
# GUARD: s1 has no missing value on any column 3c uses, so every analysis below
# rests on all 496 participants (except the gender tests, which, as in Study 1,
# leave out the three participants who gave neither male nor female).
S1P_COLS <- c("punitiveness_agg", "punit_six", "punit_five_z", "punitiveness_8item",
              "Sentence_z", "hostile_agg", "emotions_agg", "personality_agg",
              "process_agg", "crime_concerns_agg", "politid", "political_group",
              "gender", "race", "age_1", "education", "vignette")
stopifnot(all(S1P_COLS %in% names(s1)), !anyNA(s1[, S1P_COLS]), nrow(s1) == 496)
```

```{r s1p_table1}
# === 3c.1 TABLE 1: PUNITIVENESS WITH THE EIGHTEEN CORRELATES AND FIVE CLUSTERS ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: computes Table 1's last column on the six components:
# each of the eighteen correlates' and five clusters' correlation with
# punitiveness, its 95% interval, and, for the eighteen, the Benjamini-Hochberg
# corrected p (the correction H1 registered, over the eighteen tests). It also
# computes Table 1's punitiveness row: the number of parts, Cronbach's alpha,
# the mean and the SD.
# PREREG: NOT REGISTERED. Study 1's H1 is registered on its published index;
#         this is the same test on the paper's score.
# CONSUMES: s1 with punit_six (3.0); cor_ci() (section 3).
# WRITES: S1P_table1_correlations.csv (23 rows), S1P_punitiveness_scores.csv
#         (4 rows).

# The eighteen correlates and five clusters, in Table 1's order (by concept, as
# Study 1's 01_main_analysis.Rmd orders them), with the paper's labels.
S1P_CORRELATES <- c(
  crime_rates_comp = "Perceived crime rates", fear_comp = "Fear of crime",
  dueprocess_comp  = "Due-process permissiveness",
  uncertain_comp   = "Convicting on uncertain evidence",
  hatred_comp      = "Hatred", anger_comp = "Anger",
  exclusion_comp   = "Social exclusion", degradation_comp = "Degradation",
  suffering_comp   = "Infliction of suffering",
  prisonvi_comp    = "Tolerance of prison violence",
  harsh_comp       = "Harsh prison conditions", revenge_comp = "Revenge",
  rwa_comp         = "Right-wing authoritarianism",
  sdo_comp         = "Social dominance orientation",
  venge_comp       = "Trait vengefulness", vprone_comp = "Violence proneness",
  raceresent_comp  = "Racial resentment", bloodsports_comp = "Blood sports viewership")
S1P_CLUSTERS <- c(crime_concerns_agg = "Crime concerns",
                  process_agg        = "Process violations",
                  emotions_agg       = "Emotions",
                  hostile_agg        = "Hostile aggression",
                  personality_agg    = "Personality and ideology")
stopifnot(all(c(names(S1P_CORRELATES), names(S1P_CLUSTERS)) %in% names(s1)),
          !anyNA(s1[, c(names(S1P_CORRELATES), names(S1P_CLUSTERS))]))

# One row per measure: r, its Fisher-z 95% interval (cor.test(), as Study 1),
# and the two-sided p. BH is applied over the eighteen correlates only, the
# family H1 registered; the clusters are not in that family and carry no
# corrected p.
table1_col <- function(score) {
  one <- function(v, lab, kind) {
    tt <- cor.test(s1[[score]], s1[[v]])
    data.frame(measure = lab, variable = v, kind = kind, n = nrow(s1),
               r = unname(tt$estimate), ci_lower = tt$conf.int[1],
               ci_upper = tt$conf.int[2], p_two = tt$p.value)
  }
  cor18 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(S1P_CORRELATES), function(v)
    one(v, S1P_CORRELATES[[v]], "Correlate")))
  cor18$p_BH <- p.adjust(cor18$p_two, method = "BH")
  clu5 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(S1P_CLUSTERS), function(v)
    one(v, S1P_CLUSTERS[[v]], "Cluster")))
  clu5$p_BH <- NA_real_
  rbind(cor18, clu5)
}

# GUARD, published index: the eighteen r, their intervals and the BH-corrected
# p against Study 1's h1_construct_level_fdr.csv (r and interval to the three
# decimals it prints, the corrected p exactly), and the clusters against
# h2_extended_steiger.csv.
t1_old <- table1_col("punitiveness_agg")
h1fdr <- read_s1(file.path(S1_SUPP, "h1_construct_level_fdr.csv"))
h1fdr <- h1fdr[match(names(S1P_CORRELATES), h1fdr$Construct), ]
stopifnot(!anyNA(h1fdr$r),
          all(abs(round(t1_old$r[1:18], 3) - h1fdr$r) < 1e-9),
          all(abs(round(t1_old$ci_lower[1:18], 3) - h1fdr$CI_lo) < 1e-9),
          all(abs(round(t1_old$ci_upper[1:18], 3) - h1fdr$CI_hi) < 1e-9),
          isTRUE(all.equal(t1_old$p_BH[1:18], h1fdr$p_FDR, tolerance = 1e-8)))
# h2_extended_steiger.csv lists hostile aggression, emotions, personality and
# process violations in that order (checked by name), each with crime concerns'
# r beside it; section 3c.2 reads it again for the Steiger tests.
h2x_old <- read_s1(file.path(S1_ROOT, "output", "tables", "h2_extended_steiger.csv"))
stopifnot(identical(h2x_old$Cluster, c("Hostile Aggression", "Emotions",
                                       "Personality", "Process Violations")))
t1_old_clu <- setNames(t1_old$r, t1_old$variable)[c("hostile_agg", "emotions_agg",
                                                    "personality_agg", "process_agg")]
stopifnot(all(abs(round(t1_old_clu, 3) - h2x_old$r_Cluster) < 1e-9),
          abs(round(t1_old$r[t1_old$variable == "crime_concerns_agg"], 3) -
                h2x_old$r_Crime[1]) < 1e-9)

# The paper's numbers, on the six components.
t1 <- table1_col("punit_six")
# GUARDS, the verified six-component values: the eighteen correlations run from
# .166 (blood sports) to .667 (harsh prison conditions), all eighteen are
# significant after the BH correction (the largest corrected p is below .001),
# and the clusters are hostile aggression .690 [.641, .734], emotions .622,
# personality and ideology .597, process violations .558 and crime concerns
# .360.
t1_c <- t1[t1$kind == "Correlate", ]; t1_k <- t1[t1$kind == "Cluster", ]
stopifnot(round(min(t1_c$r), 3) == 0.166, round(max(t1_c$r), 3) == 0.667,
          t1_c$measure[which.min(t1_c$r)] == "Blood sports viewership",
          t1_c$measure[which.max(t1_c$r)] == "Harsh prison conditions",
          all(t1_c$p_BH < .05), max(t1_c$p_BH) < .001,
          all(abs(round(setNames(t1_k$r, t1_k$variable)[c("hostile_agg", "emotions_agg",
                    "personality_agg", "process_agg", "crime_concerns_agg")], 3) -
                  c(.690, .622, .597, .558, .360)) < 1e-9),
          round(t1_k$ci_lower[t1_k$variable == "hostile_agg"], 3) == 0.641,
          round(t1_k$ci_upper[t1_k$variable == "hostile_agg"], 3) == 0.734)
s1p_write(t1, "table1_correlations")

# --- Table 1's punitiveness row, and the scores set side by side ------------
# Cronbach's alpha of each score is the alpha of the parts exactly as that
# score averages them. For the six components: the five components and the
# sentence z-score, each standardized across the sample (the within-vignette
# z-score standardized once more, as zmean() does when it builds the score);
# the same rule as Study 2's PAPER_reliability. For the published index,
# Study 1's own construction: the eight items standardized, beside the sentence
# z-score (nine parts). check.keys = FALSE, so no part is silently reversed.
s1_alpha <- function(df) suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(
  psych::alpha(as.data.frame(df), check.keys = FALSE, warnings = FALSE)$total$raw_alpha))
s1_parts_z <- as.data.frame(scale(s1[, S1_PARTS]))
# GUARD: the five standardized components and the standardized sentence
# average exactly to the six-component score, so the alpha below describes it.
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(as.numeric(rowMeans(data.frame(s1_parts_z,
                                   s = as.numeric(scale(s1$Sentence_z))))),
                           as.numeric(s1$punit_six))))
s1p_scores <- data.frame(
  score = c("Punitiveness (six components)",
            "Punitiveness (five attitude components)",
            "Published index (eight items standardized, plus the sentence)",
            "Eight-item scale"),
  column = c("punit_six", "punit_five_z", "punitiveness_agg", "punitiveness_8item"),
  k = c(6, 5, 9, 8),
  alpha = c(s1_alpha(data.frame(s1_parts_z, s = as.numeric(scale(s1$Sentence_z)))),
            s1_alpha(s1_parts_z),
            s1_alpha(data.frame(scale(s1[, S1_ITEMS8]), s = s1$Sentence_z)),
            s1_alpha(s1[, S1_ITEMS8])),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
s1p_scores$M  <- vapply(s1p_scores$column, function(v) mean(s1[[v]]), numeric(1))
s1p_scores$SD <- vapply(s1p_scores$column, function(v) sd(s1[[v]]), numeric(1))
s1p_scores$r_with_six <- vapply(s1p_scores$column, function(v)
  cor(s1[[v]], s1$punit_six), numeric(1))
s1p_scores$r_with_published_index <- vapply(s1p_scores$column, function(v)
  cor(s1[[v]], s1$punitiveness_agg), numeric(1))
s1p_scores$r_with_eight_item <- vapply(s1p_scores$column, function(v)
  cor(s1[[v]], s1$punitiveness_8item), numeric(1))
# GUARDS. The published alphas against Study 1's reliability_alphas.csv (.836
# for the nine-part index, .842 for the eight items). The verified six-component
# values: alpha .802, SD 0.71, and .928 with the published index. A standardized
# score has mean 0, so the mean is checked to rounding error.
rel_s1 <- read_s1(file.path(S1_ROOT, "output", "tables", "reliability_alphas.csv"))
stopifnot(abs(round(s1p_scores$alpha[3], 3) -
                rel_s1$Alpha[rel_s1$Construct == "Punitiveness (9 items, w/ sentence)"]) < 1e-9,
          abs(round(s1p_scores$alpha[4], 3) -
                rel_s1$Alpha[rel_s1$Construct == "Punitiveness (8 items)"]) < 1e-9,
          round(s1p_scores$alpha[1], 3) == 0.802, round(s1p_scores$SD[1], 2) == 0.71,
          abs(s1p_scores$M[1]) < 1e-12,
          round(s1p_scores$r_with_published_index[1], 3) == 0.928)
s1p_write(s1p_scores, "punitiveness_scores")
knitr::kable(t1, digits = 3, caption = "Study 1, Table 1's last column on the six components")
knitr::kable(s1p_scores, digits = 3, caption = "Study 1's punitiveness scores")
```

```{r s1p_h2}
# === 3c.2 H2, THE OTHER CLUSTERS, TABLE S1 AND THE CHECK WITHOUT PARSIMONY ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES, on the six components:
#   A. Each cluster's correlation with punitiveness against crime concerns'
#      (Steiger's Z, two-sided, as Study 1's manuscript reports it): hostile
#      aggression (H2), emotions, personality and ideology, process violations.
#   B. Table S1: the same test at three levels of strictness (all six hostility
#      constructs; four, without suffering and harsh conditions; exclusion and
#      revenge only), each with the 95% BCa bootstrap interval of the
#      difference from 10,000 resamples. The first level's interval is H2's.
#   C. H2 with the two parsimony items left out of punitiveness.
# PREREG: NOT REGISTERED on this score. H2 is registered on the published
#         index; A to C repeat Study 1's own tests (its 01 section 6.2 and its
#         03 Phases 2 to 4) on the paper's score.
# CONSUMES: s1 with punit_six, hostile_cons and hostile_strict (sections 3.0
#           and 3); s1p_steiger(), s1p_write(), read_s1(), S1_SUPP (3c.0);
#           h2x_old, Study 1's h2_extended_steiger.csv (3c.1); zmean() (3.0);
#           LEVELS (section 3).
# WRITES: S1P_H2_steiger.csv (4 rows), S1P_tableS1_strictness.csv (3 rows),
#         S1P_parsimony_check.csv (1 row).

# --- A. Each cluster against crime concerns ---------------------------------
H2_CLUSTERS <- c(hostile_agg = "Hostile aggression", emotions_agg = "Emotions",
                 personality_agg = "Personality and ideology",
                 process_agg = "Process violations")
h2_table <- function(score) do.call(rbind, lapply(names(H2_CLUSTERS), function(v)
  cbind(comparison = paste(H2_CLUSTERS[[v]], "vs crime concerns"),
        s1p_steiger(s1, score, v, "crime_concerns_agg"))))
# GUARD, published index: the differences against Study 1's
# h2_extended_steiger.csv (three decimals), its two-sided p for personality
# (.0012) and process violations (.0091) to the four decimals it prints, and
# H2's Z of 6.26 from the manuscript.
h2_old <- h2_table("punitiveness_agg")
stopifnot(all(abs(round(h2_old$diff, 3) - h2x_old$Difference) < 1e-9),
          all(abs(round(h2_old$p_two[3:4], 4) - h2x_old$Steiger_p[3:4]) < 1e-9),
          round(h2_old$z[1], 2) == 6.26)
h2 <- h2_table("punit_six")
# GUARD, the verified six-component values: H2 .690 against .360, a difference
# of .331 with Z = 8.54; emotions Z = 6.71; personality and ideology Z = 5.42.
stopifnot(round(h2$r_jk[1], 3) == 0.690, round(h2$r_jh[1], 3) == 0.360,
          round(h2$diff[1], 3) == 0.331, round(h2$z[1], 2) == 8.54,
          round(h2$z[2], 2) == 6.71, round(h2$z[3], 2) == 5.42,
          all(h2$p_two < .05))
names(h2)[names(h2) == "r_jk"] <- "r_cluster"
names(h2)[names(h2) == "r_jh"] <- "r_crime"
names(h2)[names(h2) == "r_kh"] <- "r_cluster_with_crime"
s1p_write(h2, "H2_steiger")

# --- B. Table S1: three levels of strictness, with BCa intervals -------------
# THE BOOTSTRAP, exactly as Study 1's 03_supplementary_analyses.Rmd (Phase 3)
# runs it: the seed is set to 42 once, then boot::boot() draws 10,000 resamples
# of participants for each level in turn (all six constructs, then four, then
# two), and boot::boot.ci() gives the bias-corrected and accelerated (BCa)
# interval. Because the three levels draw from one random stream in that order,
# the ORDER OF THE RUNS matters: the same seed and order reproduce Study 1's
# published intervals exactly. The published index is run first, from seed 42,
# and checked against Study 1's export; the six components are then run from
# seed 42 again, so both scorings are judged on the same resamples.
# The statistic is Study 1's make_h2_boot_fn(): in each resample, the
# correlation of punitiveness with the hostility composite minus its
# correlation with crime concerns (use = "p" as there; no value is missing).
S1P_BOOT_R    <- 10000
S1P_BOOT_SEED <- 42
S1P_TARGETS   <- c("hostile_agg", "hostile_cons", "hostile_strict")
boot_levels <- function(score) {
  bd <- s1[, c(score, S1P_TARGETS, "crime_concerns_agg")]
  set.seed(S1P_BOOT_SEED)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(S1P_TARGETS), function(i) {
    tg <- S1P_TARGETS[i]
    fn <- function(data, idx) {
      x <- data[idx, ]
      cor(x[[score]], x[[tg]], use = "p") - cor(x[[score]], x$crime_concerns_agg, use = "p")
    }
    br <- boot::boot(data = bd, statistic = fn, R = S1P_BOOT_R)
    ci <- boot::boot.ci(br, type = "bca")
    st <- s1p_steiger(s1, score, tg, "crime_concerns_agg")
    rc <- cor.test(s1[[score]], s1[[tg]])
    data.frame(level = LEVELS[i], n = nrow(bd), r_hostile = st$r_jk,
               r_hostile_lower = rc$conf.int[1], r_hostile_upper = rc$conf.int[2],
               r_crime = st$r_jh, diff = st$diff, z = st$z, p_two = st$p_two,
               bca_lower = ci$bca[4], bca_upper = ci$bca[5],
               boot_se = sd(br$t), resamples = S1P_BOOT_R)
  }))
}
# GUARD, published index: every observed difference, BCa limit and bootstrap SE
# against Study 1's tautology_bootstrap_cis.csv (to the three decimals it
# prints: [.174, .367], [.134, .331], [.125, .323]), and r and Z against its
# tautology_steiger_by_level.csv.
lev_old <- boot_levels("punitiveness_agg")
tb <- read_s1(file.path(S1_SUPP, "tautology_bootstrap_cis.csv"))
ts <- read_s1(file.path(S1_SUPP, "tautology_steiger_by_level.csv"))
stopifnot(all(abs(round(lev_old$diff, 3) - tb$Observed_Diff) < 1e-9),
          all(abs(round(lev_old$bca_lower, 3) - tb$BCa_Lower) < 1e-9),
          all(abs(round(lev_old$bca_upper, 3) - tb$BCa_Upper) < 1e-9),
          all(abs(round(lev_old$boot_se, 3) - tb$Boot_SE) < 1e-9),
          all(abs(round(lev_old$r_hostile, 3) - ts$r_Hostile) < 1e-9),
          all(abs(round(lev_old$z, 2) - ts$Z) < 1e-9),
          isTRUE(all.equal(lev_old$p_two, ts$p, tolerance = 1e-6)))
lev <- boot_levels("punit_six")
# GUARD, the verified six-component values: all six constructs .331 [.240,
# .431]; four .286 [.193, .391], Z = 6.90; two .263 [.166, .366], Z = 6.38;
# every interval above zero.
stopifnot(all(abs(round(lev$diff, 3) - c(.331, .286, .263)) < 1e-9),
          all(abs(round(lev$bca_lower, 3) - c(.240, .193, .166)) < 1e-9),
          all(abs(round(lev$bca_upper, 3) - c(.431, .391, .366)) < 1e-9),
          all(abs(round(lev$z, 2) - c(8.54, 6.90, 6.38)) < 1e-9),
          all(lev$bca_lower > 0),
          isTRUE(all.equal(lev$diff[1], h2$diff[1])))
s1p_write(lev, "tableS1_strictness")

# --- C. H2 without the parsimony items ----------------------------------------
# Study 1's check (03, Phase 4) rebuilt its published index without the two
# parsimony items: the four remaining components standardized and averaged,
# that average and the sentence z-score standardized and averaged. The
# six-component analogue drops the parsimony component and weights the five
# remaining parts (four attitude components and the sentence) equally.
np_old <- rowMeans(scale(cbind(
  rowMeans(scale(s1[, c("punishmore_comp", "threestrikes_comp", "LWOP", "deathpenalty")])),
  s1$Sentence_z)))
np_six <- zmean(s1$punishmore_comp, s1$threestrikes_comp, s1$LWOP, s1$deathpenalty,
                s1$Sentence_z)
s1_np <- data.frame(np_old = np_old, np_six = np_six, hostile_agg = s1$hostile_agg,
                    crime_concerns_agg = s1$crime_concerns_agg)
# GUARD, published index: r .581 and .334 and Z = 5.87, Study 1's
# parsimony_sensitivity.csv (second row).
ps_old <- s1p_steiger(s1_np, "np_old", "hostile_agg", "crime_concerns_agg")
psx <- read_s1(file.path(S1_SUPP, "parsimony_sensitivity.csv"))
stopifnot(abs(round(ps_old$r_jk, 3) - psx$r_Hostile[2]) < 1e-9,
          abs(round(ps_old$r_jh, 3) - psx$r_Crime[2]) < 1e-9,
          abs(round(ps_old$z, 2) - psx$Z[2]) < 1e-9)
ps_six <- s1p_steiger(s1_np, "np_six", "hostile_agg", "crime_concerns_agg")
# GUARD, the verified six-component values: .681 against .374, Z = 7.90.
stopifnot(round(ps_six$r_jk, 3) == 0.681, round(ps_six$r_jh, 3) == 0.374,
          round(ps_six$z, 2) == 7.90)
s1p_write(cbind(check = "Punitiveness without the parsimony component (five parts)",
                ps_six), "parsimony_check")

cat("Published index, reproduced:\n")
print(lev_old[, c("level", "diff", "bca_lower", "bca_upper", "z")], digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(h2, digits = 4, caption = "Study 1, each cluster against crime concerns (six components)")
knitr::kable(lev, digits = 3, caption = "Study 1, Table S1 on the six components")
```

```{r s1p_moderation}
# === 3c.3 TABLES S2 AND S3: DO DEMOGRAPHICS MODERATE THE CORRELATES? ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: reruns Study 1's demographic moderation tests (its
# 03_supplementary_analyses.Rmd, Phase 7) with the paper's scores. Four
# correlates (hostile aggression, crime concerns, right-wing authoritarianism,
# racial resentment), each standardized, are crossed with six moderators (age,
# gender, race White or not, race in seven categories, education, political
# orientation): 24 models per table.
#   Table S2: the outcome is punitiveness (the six components).
#   Table S3: the outcome is the sentence (Sentence_z) and punitiveness enters as
#             a standardized covariate. The sentence is the outcome, so the
#             covariate must leave it out: the five attitude components, each
#             standardized (D2; Study 1's own run used the eight-item scale).
# Each row is the interaction's coefficient b (in units of the outcome) and its
# p, or, for the seven-category race factor, which has six interaction terms,
# the joint F test from car::Anova(type = 3), as Study 1 did. The BH correction
# runs over the 24 tests of each table.
# PREREG: NOT REGISTERED (exploratory in Study 1 as well).
# CONSUMES: s1 with punit_six and punit_five_z (3.0); s1p_write() (3c.0).
# WRITES: S1P_tableS2_moderation.csv, S1P_tableS3_moderation.csv (24 rows each).

# The moderators, coded exactly as Study 1's Phase 7 codes them: race White (1)
# against everyone else; race in its seven categories; gender as male (1) or
# female (2), with the three who gave another answer set to missing (so those
# models have 493 participants); age, education and political orientation
# (1 to 7) standardized. s1m is a copy, so s1 itself is unchanged.
s1m <- s1
s1m$race_dichot <- factor(ifelse(s1m$race == 1, "White", "NonWhite"),
                          levels = c("White", "NonWhite"))
s1m$race_factor <- factor(s1m$race, levels = 1:7,
                          labels = c("White", "Black", "Asian", "Hispanic",
                                     "NativeAm", "PacIslander", "Other"))
s1m$gender_binary <- factor(ifelse(s1m$gender == 1, "Male",
                                   ifelse(s1m$gender == 2, "Female", NA)),
                            levels = c("Male", "Female"))
s1m$education_z <- as.numeric(scale(s1m$education))
s1m$age_z       <- as.numeric(scale(s1m$age_1))
s1m$politid_z   <- as.numeric(scale(s1m$politid))
stopifnot(sum(is.na(s1m$gender_binary)) == 3, !anyNA(s1m$race_factor))

MOD_TARGETS <- c(hostile_agg = "Hostile aggression", crime_concerns_agg = "Crime concerns",
                 rwa_comp = "Right-wing authoritarianism", raceresent_comp = "Racial resentment")
MOD_MODS <- c(age_z = "Age", gender_binary = "Gender (women vs men)",
              race_dichot = "Race (non-White vs White)",
              race_factor = "Race (seven categories)", education_z = "Education",
              politid_z = "Political orientation")
# One model, exactly as Study 1's run_moderation() and
# run_moderation_with_control() fit it: outcome ~ [control_z +] target_z * mod.
run_mod <- function(outcome, target, mod, control = NULL) {
  dd <- s1m
  dd$target_z <- as.numeric(scale(dd[[target]]))
  if (!is.null(control)) dd$control_z <- as.numeric(scale(dd[[control]]))
  fml <- as.formula(sprintf("%s ~ %starget_z * %s", outcome,
                            if (is.null(control)) "" else "control_z + ", mod))
  fit <- lm(fml, data = dd)
  cf <- summary(fit)$coefficients
  inter <- grep(":", rownames(cf), value = TRUE)
  out <- data.frame(target = MOD_TARGETS[[target]], moderator = MOD_MODS[[mod]],
                    n = nobs(fit), b_target = cf["target_z", "Estimate"],
                    test = NA_character_, b_interaction = NA_real_, F = NA_real_,
                    df_num = NA_real_, df_den = fit$df.residual, p = NA_real_,
                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  if (length(inter) > 1) {
    # Several interaction terms (the seven race categories): one joint F test.
    a <- car::Anova(fit, type = 3)
    lab <- paste("target_z", mod, sep = ":")
    out$test <- "joint F (type 3)"; out$F <- a[lab, "F value"]
    out$df_num <- a[lab, "Df"]; out$p <- a[lab, "Pr(>F)"]
  } else {
    out$test <- "t on the interaction"; out$b_interaction <- cf[inter, "Estimate"]
    out$df_num <- 1; out$p <- cf[inter, "Pr(>|t|)"]
  }
  out
}
mod_table <- function(outcome, control = NULL) {
  o <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(MOD_TARGETS), function(t)
    do.call(rbind, lapply(names(MOD_MODS), function(m) run_mod(outcome, t, m, control)))))
  o$p_BH <- p.adjust(o$p, method = "BH")
  o$outcome <- outcome
  o$covariate <- if (is.null(control)) "" else control
  o
}
# GUARD, published index: all 24 rows of each table against Study 1's exports
# (interactions_punitiveness_agg.csv, interactions_sentence_z.csv), in the same
# order: n, b to the three decimals the export prints, p and corrected p to
# rounding error, and F to its two decimals.
same_as_export <- function(mine, theirs) {
  stopifnot(nrow(mine) == 24, nrow(theirs) == 24,
            all(mine$n == theirs$n),
            all(is.na(mine$b_interaction) == is.na(theirs$b_inter)),
            all(abs(round(mine$b_interaction, 3) - theirs$b_inter) < 1e-9, na.rm = TRUE),
            isTRUE(all.equal(mine$p, theirs$p_inter, tolerance = 1e-8)),
            isTRUE(all.equal(mine$p_BH, theirs$p_inter_FDR, tolerance = 1e-8)),
            all(abs(round(mine$F, 2) - theirs$F_omnibus) < 1e-9, na.rm = TRUE))
}
same_as_export(mod_table("punitiveness_agg"),
               read_s1(file.path(S1_SUPP, "interactions_punitiveness_agg.csv")))
same_as_export(mod_table("Sentence_z", control = "punitiveness_8item"),
               read_s1(file.path(S1_SUPP, "interactions_sentence_z.csv")))

# The paper's tables.
tS2 <- mod_table("punit_six")
tS3 <- mod_table("Sentence_z", control = "punit_five_z")
# GUARDS, the verified six-component values. Table S2: exactly two interactions
# survive the correction, crime concerns x age (b = .159) and hostile
# aggression x political orientation (b = -.072, p = .00058, corrected p =
# .0069). Table S3: none of the 24.
s2_sig <- tS2[tS2$p_BH < .05, ]
row_ca <- tS2[tS2$target == "Crime concerns" & tS2$moderator == "Age", ]
row_hp <- tS2[tS2$target == "Hostile aggression" & tS2$moderator == "Political orientation", ]
stopifnot(nrow(s2_sig) == 2,
          setequal(paste(s2_sig$target, s2_sig$moderator),
                   c("Crime concerns Age", "Hostile aggression Political orientation")),
          round(row_ca$b_interaction, 3) == 0.159,
          round(row_hp$b_interaction, 3) == -0.072,
          round(row_hp$p, 5) == 0.00058, round(row_hp$p_BH, 4) == 0.0069,
          sum(tS3$p_BH < .05) == 0)
s1p_write(tS2, "tableS2_moderation")
s1p_write(tS3, "tableS3_moderation")
knitr::kable(tS2, digits = 4, caption = "Study 1, Table S2 on the six components")
knitr::kable(tS3, digits = 4, caption = "Study 1, Table S3 with the five components as covariate")
```

```{r s1p_levels}
# === 3c.4 SECTION S1: PUNITIVENESS BY POLITICAL GROUP, GENDER, RACE, AGE AND
# EDUCATION ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: reruns Study 1's comparisons of the LEVEL of
# punitiveness across demographic groups (its 03, Phase 7 descriptives) on the
# six components: the mean in each political group, a one-way analysis of
# variance across the three groups, Cohen's d for conservatives against
# liberals and the correlation with the 1-to-7 political item; women against men
# and non-White against White participants by Welch's t test with Cohen's d;
# and the correlations with age and education.
# PREREG: NOT REGISTERED (descriptive context in Study 1 as well).
# CONSUMES: s1m (3c.3); s1p_write() (3c.0).
# WRITES: S1P_levels.csv (one row per statistic).

# Cohen's d with the pooled SD, Study 1's helper.
cohen_d <- function(x1, x2) {
  x1 <- x1[!is.na(x1)]; x2 <- x2[!is.na(x2)]
  n1 <- length(x1); n2 <- length(x2)
  (mean(x1) - mean(x2)) / sqrt(((n1 - 1) * var(x1) + (n2 - 1) * var(x2)) / (n1 + n2 - 2))
}
levels_run <- function(score) {
  y <- s1m[[score]]
  pol_aov <- summary(aov(y ~ s1m$political_group))[[1]]
  pol_r   <- cor.test(s1m$politid, y)
  g_m <- y[s1m$gender_binary == "Male"]; g_f <- y[s1m$gender_binary == "Female"]
  gen_t <- t.test(g_f, g_m)                         # women minus men, Welch
  r_w <- y[s1m$race_dichot == "White"]; r_nw <- y[s1m$race_dichot == "NonWhite"]
  race_t <- t.test(r_nw, r_w)                       # non-White minus White, Welch
  age_r <- cor.test(s1m$age_1, y); edu_r <- cor.test(s1m$education, y)
  pm <- tapply(y, s1m$political_group, mean)
  list(
    table = data.frame(
      demographic = c(rep("Political orientation", 9), rep("Gender", 6),
                      rep("Race", 6), rep("Age", 2), rep("Education", 2)),
      statistic = c("M, liberals", "M, moderates", "M, conservatives",
                    "F (one-way ANOVA, three groups)", "df1", "df2", "p (ANOVA)",
                    "d, conservatives minus liberals", "r with the 1-to-7 item",
                    "M, men", "M, women", "t (Welch, women minus men)", "df", "p",
                    "d, women minus men",
                    "M, White", "M, non-White", "t (Welch, non-White minus White)", "df",
                    "p", "d, non-White minus White",
                    "r", "p", "r", "p"),
      value = c(pm[["Liberal"]], pm[["Moderate"]], pm[["Conservative"]],
                pol_aov$`F value`[1], pol_aov$Df[1], pol_aov$Df[2], pol_aov$`Pr(>F)`[1],
                cohen_d(y[s1m$political_group == "Conservative"],
                        y[s1m$political_group == "Liberal"]),
                unname(pol_r$estimate),
                mean(g_m, na.rm = TRUE), mean(g_f, na.rm = TRUE),
                unname(gen_t$statistic), unname(gen_t$parameter), gen_t$p.value,
                cohen_d(g_f, g_m),
                mean(r_w), mean(r_nw), unname(race_t$statistic),
                unname(race_t$parameter), race_t$p.value, cohen_d(r_nw, r_w),
                unname(age_r$estimate), age_r$p.value,
                unname(edu_r$estimate), edu_r$p.value),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
    # The same results as Study 1's export formats them, for the guard.
    stat = c(sprintf("F(%d,%d)=%.2f", pol_aov$Df[1], pol_aov$Df[2], pol_aov$`F value`[1]),
             sprintf("t(%.0f)=%.2f", gen_t$parameter, gen_t$statistic),
             sprintf("t(%.0f)=%.2f", race_t$parameter, race_t$statistic),
             sprintf("r=%.3f", age_r$estimate), sprintf("r=%.3f", edu_r$estimate)),
    p = round(c(pol_aov$`Pr(>F)`[1], gen_t$p.value, race_t$p.value,
                age_r$p.value, edu_r$p.value), 4),
    means = pm)
}
# GUARD, published index: every test statistic, its degrees of freedom and its
# p against Study 1's punitiveness_levels_by_demographic.csv (formatted and
# rounded exactly as that file prints them), and the three political means
# against punitiveness_means_political.csv.
lv_old <- levels_run("punitiveness_agg")
lvx <- read_s1(file.path(S1_SUPP, "punitiveness_levels_by_demographic.csv"))
pmx <- read_s1(file.path(S1_SUPP, "punitiveness_means_political.csv"))
stopifnot(identical(lv_old$stat, lvx$Stat),
          all(abs(lv_old$p - lvx$p) < 1e-9),
          isTRUE(all.equal(as.numeric(lv_old$means[pmx$political_group]), pmx$M,
                           tolerance = 1e-10)))
lv <- levels_run("punit_six")
lvt <- lv$table
getv <- function(dem, st) lvt$value[lvt$demographic == dem & lvt$statistic == st]
# GUARDS, the verified six-component values: politics F(2, 493) = 39.13,
# d = 0.90, r = .43; gender t(490) = 1.97, p = .049, d = 0.18.
stopifnot(round(getv("Political orientation", "F (one-way ANOVA, three groups)"), 2) == 39.13,
          getv("Political orientation", "df1") == 2,
          getv("Political orientation", "df2") == 493,
          round(getv("Political orientation", "d, conservatives minus liberals"), 2) == 0.90,
          round(getv("Political orientation", "r with the 1-to-7 item"), 2) == 0.43,
          round(getv("Gender", "t (Welch, women minus men)"), 2) == 1.97,
          round(getv("Gender", "df")) == 490,
          round(getv("Gender", "p"), 3) == 0.049,
          round(getv("Gender", "d, women minus men"), 2) == 0.18)
s1p_write(lvt, "levels")
knitr::kable(lvt, digits = 4, caption = "Study 1, punitiveness (six components) by demographic group")
```

```{r s1p_vignettes}
# === 3c.5 SECTION S1: THE CORRELATIONS ACROSS THE THREE VIGNETTES ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: on the six components, each of the eighteen correlates'
# correlation with punitiveness within each of Study 1's three vignettes; the
# range of each correlate's three correlations; the median of the eighteen
# ranges; the smallest within-vignette correlation; and the variance between
# vignettes in a mixed model with a random intercept for vignette.
# COMPUTED AS STUDY 1 DID (its 01_main_analysis.Rmd, sections 8.2 and 8.3): each
# within-vignette correlation is rounded to two decimals BEFORE the range is
# taken, and the median is the median of those ranges; the mixed model is
# punitiveness ~ hostile_agg + (1 | vignette), fitted by lme4::lmer() with its
# default (REML). Because rounding first can move a median that falls between
# two rounding points, the unrounded median and smallest r are reported beside
# them.
# PREREG: NOT REGISTERED (a robustness check in Study 1 as well).
# CONSUMES: s1 with punit_six (3.0); S1P_CORRELATES (3c.1); s1p_write() (3c.0).
# WRITES: S1P_vignette_stability.csv (18 rows), S1P_vignette_summary.csv.
vig_table <- function(score) {
  v <- t(sapply(names(S1P_CORRELATES), function(x)
    sapply(1:3, function(k) with(s1[s1$vignette == k, ], cor(get(score), get(x))))))
  colnames(v) <- c("r_vignette_A", "r_vignette_B", "r_vignette_C")
  v_round <- round(v, 2)
  data.frame(measure = unname(S1P_CORRELATES), variable = names(S1P_CORRELATES),
             v, range_study1_method = apply(v_round, 1, function(z) max(z) - min(z)),
             range_unrounded = apply(v, 1, function(z) max(z) - min(z)),
             row.names = NULL, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}
mixed_var <- function(score) {
  m <- suppressMessages(suppressWarnings(lme4::lmer(
    as.formula(paste(score, "~ hostile_agg + (1 | vignette)")), data = s1)))
  vc <- as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(m))
  c(between = vc$vcov[vc$grp == "vignette"], residual = vc$vcov[vc$grp == "Residual"],
    singular = as.numeric(lme4::isSingular(m)))
}
# GUARD, published index: every within-vignette correlation, rounded to two
# decimals, against Study 1's vignette_correlation_stability.csv; the median
# range of .135 (the draft prints .13); and a between-vignette variance of zero
# (a singular fit), as Study 1 found.
S1_STAB_NAMES <- c("Crime Rates" = "crime_rates_comp", "Fear" = "fear_comp",
                   "Due Process" = "dueprocess_comp", "Uncertain Evidence" = "uncertain_comp",
                   "Hatred" = "hatred_comp", "Anger" = "anger_comp",
                   "Exclusion" = "exclusion_comp", "Degradation" = "degradation_comp",
                   "Suffering" = "suffering_comp", "Prison Violence" = "prisonvi_comp",
                   "Harsh Conditions" = "harsh_comp", "Revenge" = "revenge_comp",
                   "RWA" = "rwa_comp", "SDO" = "sdo_comp", "Vengefulness" = "venge_comp",
                   "Violence Proneness" = "vprone_comp",
                   "Racial Resentment" = "raceresent_comp", "Blood Sports" = "bloodsports_comp")
vs_x <- read_s1(file.path(S1_ROOT, "output", "tables", "vignette_correlation_stability.csv"))
stopifnot(setequal(vs_x$Construct, names(S1_STAB_NAMES)),
          setequal(unname(S1_STAB_NAMES), names(S1P_CORRELATES)))
vig_old <- vig_table("punitiveness_agg")
vs_x <- vs_x[match(names(S1P_CORRELATES), S1_STAB_NAMES[vs_x$Construct]), ]
stopifnot(all(abs(round(as.matrix(vig_old[, c("r_vignette_A", "r_vignette_B", "r_vignette_C")]), 2) -
                  as.matrix(vs_x[, c("Vignette_1", "Vignette_2", "Vignette_3")])) < 1e-9),
          round(median(vig_old$range_study1_method), 3) == 0.135)
mm_old <- mixed_var("punitiveness_agg")
stopifnot(mm_old[["between"]] < 1e-10, mm_old[["singular"]] == 1)

vig <- vig_table("punit_six")
mm  <- mixed_var("punit_six")
vr  <- as.matrix(vig[, c("r_vignette_A", "r_vignette_B", "r_vignette_C")])
# GUARDS, the verified six-component values: median range .090 by Study 1's
# method (.088 unrounded); smallest within-vignette correlation .076 (fear of
# crime; .08 rounded); no correlate negative in any vignette; no variance
# between vignettes.
stopifnot(round(median(vig$range_study1_method), 3) == 0.090,
          round(median(vig$range_unrounded), 3) == 0.088,
          round(min(vr), 3) == 0.076,
          vig$measure[which.min(apply(vr, 1, min))] == "Fear of crime",
          all(vr > 0), mm[["between"]] < 1e-10)
vig_summary <- data.frame(
  quantity = c("Median range across the three vignettes (Study 1's method: rounded r)",
               "Median range across the three vignettes (unrounded r)",
               "Largest range (Study 1's method)",
               "Smallest within-vignette r (rounded to two decimals)",
               "Smallest within-vignette r (unrounded)",
               "Within-vignette correlations below zero (of 54)",
               "Mixed model: variance between vignettes",
               "Mixed model: residual variance",
               "Mixed model: singular fit (1 = yes)"),
  value = c(median(vig$range_study1_method), median(vig$range_unrounded),
            max(vig$range_study1_method), min(round(vr, 2)), min(vr), sum(vr < 0),
            mm[["between"]], mm[["residual"]], mm[["singular"]]),
  detail = c("", "", vig$measure[which.max(vig$range_study1_method)],
             vig$measure[which.min(apply(vr, 1, min))],
             vig$measure[which.min(apply(vr, 1, min))], "",
             "punit_six ~ hostile_agg + (1 | vignette), REML", "", ""),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
s1p_write(vig, "vignette_stability")
s1p_write(vig_summary, "vignette_summary")
knitr::kable(vig_summary, digits = 4, caption = "Study 1, the correlations across vignettes (six components)")
```
