# 4. Study 2, read from its own exports

```{r study2_scores}
# === 4.0 STUDY 2'S PUNITIVENESS: THE PAPER'S TWO SCORES ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: adds the paper's two punitiveness scores to s2 for every
# participant, from 01_main_analysis.Rmd's export PAPER_person_scores (section
# 9.19A), and rebuilds both from the items here as an independent check.
#   s2$punit_six     the six components weighted equally (01's punit_parts6,
#                    section 7.4): the paper's punitiveness in the main text.
#   s2$punit_five_z  the five attitude components, each standardized, averaged
#                    (01's punit_parts5z): the paper's punitiveness where the
#                    sentence or the sentencing ratio is on the other side.
# PREREG: NOT REGISTERED. The registered scores (punitiveness, the eight-item
#         scale; punitiveness_full, the full index) stay in s2 unchanged, and
#         section 2's guards and every registered number read them.
# CONSUMES: s2, read_s2() (section 1); zmean() (section 3.0).
ps2 <- read_s2("PAPER_person_scores")
# GUARD: the export has one row per analyzed participant, no duplicate and no
# missing score, and its participants are s2's, in s2's order.
stopifnot(nrow(ps2) == 948, !anyDuplicated(ps2$ResponseId),
          !anyNA(ps2[, c("punit_six", "punit_five_z", "desert_theory", "just_deserts")]),
          identical(ps2$ResponseId, s2$ResponseId))
s2$punit_six    <- ps2$punit_six
s2$punit_five_z <- ps2$punit_five_z

# GUARD: the same two scores rebuilt here from the items, exactly as 01's
# section 7.4 builds them (each two-item component the mean of its items after
# reverse coding; the one-item components as answered; the sentence as its
# within-vignette z-score; zmean() over the parts). They must agree with the
# export to rounding error. Every item was required, so no part is missing.
S2_ITEMS8 <- c("punishmore_1_R", "punishmore_2", "parsimony_1_R", "parsimony_2_R",
               "threestrikes_1", "threestrikes_2", "LWOP", "deathpenalty")
stopifnot(!anyNA(s2[, c(S2_ITEMS8, "Sentence1_z")]))
s2_parts <- data.frame(
  punish_more        = rowMeans(s2[, c("punishmore_1_R", "punishmore_2")]),
  parsimony_rejected = rowMeans(s2[, c("parsimony_1_R", "parsimony_2_R")]),
  three_strikes      = rowMeans(s2[, c("threestrikes_1", "threestrikes_2")]),
  life_without_parole = as.numeric(s2$LWOP),
  death_penalty      = as.numeric(s2$deathpenalty))
stopifnot(max(abs(zmean(s2_parts, s2$Sentence1_z) - s2$punit_six)) < 1e-10,
          max(abs(zmean(s2_parts) - s2$punit_five_z)) < 1e-10)
# GUARD: the agreement 01 guards (section 9.19A): six components .945 with the
# registered full index and .972 with the eight-item scale; five components .99
# with the eight-item scale.
stopifnot(round(cor(s2$punit_six, s2$punitiveness_full), 3) == 0.945,
          round(cor(s2$punit_six, s2$punitiveness), 3) == 0.972,
          round(cor(s2$punit_five_z, s2$punitiveness), 2) == 0.99)
cat(sprintf(paste("Study 2: six components vs the registered full index r = %.3f;",
                  "vs the eight-item scale r = %.3f;",
                  "five components vs the eight-item scale r = %.3f.\n"),
            cor(s2$punit_six, s2$punitiveness_full), cor(s2$punit_six, s2$punitiveness),
            cor(s2$punit_five_z, s2$punitiveness)))
```

```{r study2}
# === STUDY 2 QUANTITIES ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: reads every Study 2 number from the tables
# 01_main_analysis.Rmd wrote. Where a number needed here was never exported (the
# comparisons between clusters), the clusters are rebuilt from the raw items and
# checked against the exported correlations before any comparison is run.
# PUNITIVENESS is the six components (s2$punit_six), matching Study 1's side
# (section 3): 01's DS_ exports (sections 7.5 and 7.6) label that score FULL
# below. EIGHT is the eight-item scale, used only for the comparison of the two
# studies on the attitude items alone (part B).
# PREREG: NOT REGISTERED (the paper's scoring; see sections 3.0 and 4.0).
# CONSUMES: read_s2(), s2 with punit_six (4.0); s1_con, s1_eight, s1_clusters,
#           LEVELS, PARTS, shared_personality_items (section 3).
FULL  <- "Punitiveness (six components)"
EIGHT <- "Punitiveness (8 items)"
s2_label <- c("Harsh prison conditions", "Hatred", "Social exclusion",
              "Infliction of suffering", "Due-process permissiveness",
              "Degradation", "Anger", "Perceived crime rates",
              "Tolerance of prison violence", "Convicting on uncertain evidence",
              "Fear of crime")
pers_label <- c("Right-Wing Authoritarianism" = "Right-wing authoritarianism",
                "Social Dominance Orientation" = "Social dominance orientation",
                "Racial resentment" = "Racial resentment",
                "Violence proneness" = "Violence proneness")
keep <- c("construct", "r", "ci_lower", "ci_upper", "n")

# --- A. The sixteen constructs, six components -------------------------------
# Eleven come from the registered correlate family on the six components
# (PAPER_H1, section 9.19B). The four-item revenge row is DROPPED and replaced
# by the three-item row, which is the one that matches Study 1's scale.
h1f <- read_s2("PAPER_H1")
h1f <- h1f[h1f$y != "Revenge", ]
stopifnot(nrow(h1f) == 11, setequal(h1f$y, s2_label))
h1f$construct <- h1f$y
# GUARD: PAPER_H1 is on the six components: its harsh-conditions row equals the
# correlation recomputed here from s2$punit_six.
same_r <- function(a, b) isTRUE(all.equal(a, b, tolerance = 1e-10))
stopifnot(same_r(h1f$r[h1f$y == "Harsh prison conditions"], cor(s2$punit_six, s2$harsh)))
pers <- read_s2("DS_personality_correlates")
pers_f <- pers[pers$x == FULL, ]
stopifnot(nrow(pers_f) == 4, all(pers_f$y %in% names(pers_label)))
pers_f$construct <- unname(pers_label[pers_f$y])
rev3 <- read_s2("DS_revenge_darkside")
rev3_f <- rev3[rev3$x == FULL & grepl("Dark Side scoring", rev3$y), ]
stopifnot(nrow(rev3_f) == 1)
rev3_f$construct <- "Revenge (three shared items)"
s2_con <- rbind(h1f[, keep], pers_f[, keep], rev3_f[, keep])
# GUARD: the same sixteen constructs in both studies, no more and no fewer.
stopifnot(nrow(s2_con) == 16, setequal(s2_con$construct, s1_con$construct))

# --- B. The same twelve on the eight-item scale -----------------------------
h1e <- read_s2("H1_correlations")
h1e <- h1e[h1e$y != "Revenge", ]
h1e$construct <- h1e$y
rev3_e <- rev3[rev3$x == EIGHT & grepl("Dark Side scoring", rev3$y), ]
stopifnot(nrow(h1e) == 11, nrow(rev3_e) == 1)
rev3_e$construct <- "Revenge (three shared items)"
s2_eight <- rbind(h1e[, keep], rev3_e[, keep])
stopifnot(setequal(s2_eight$construct, s1_eight$construct))

# --- C. The clusters, the levels, the parts ----------------------------------
clu <- read_s2("DS_cluster_correlations")
s2_clu <- clu[clu$x == FULL, c("y", "r", "ci_lower", "ci_upper", "n")]
names(s2_clu)[1] <- "cluster"
stopifnot(setequal(s2_clu$cluster, unname(s1_clusters)))
s2_ladder <- read_s2("DS_tautology_ladder")
# The levels are relabelled only after checking that each row is the level the
# label names, so a reordering in 01_main_analysis.Rmd cannot mislabel them.
stopifnot(nrow(s2_ladder) == 3, grepl("^All six", s2_ladder$rung[1]),
          grepl("^Four", s2_ladder$rung[2]),
          grepl("exclusion and revenge", s2_ladder$rung[3]))
s2_ladder$row <- LEVELS
# GUARD: the ladder is on the six components: its top rung's correlation with
# punitiveness is the hostile aggression cluster's in DS_cluster_correlations
# (six-component row), and every rung shares crime concerns' r with it.
stopifnot(same_r(s2_ladder$r_jk[1], s2_clu$r[s2_clu$cluster == "Hostile aggression"]),
          all(vapply(s2_ladder$r_jh, same_r, logical(1),
                     b = s2_clu$r[s2_clu$cluster == "Crime concerns"])))
s2_bypart <- read_s2("DS_H2_by_part")
s2_bypart$outcome[s2_bypart$outcome == "Parsimony rejected"] <- "Rejection of parsimony"
stopifnot(nrow(s2_bypart) == 6, setequal(s2_bypart$outcome, unname(PARTS)))
s2_bypart <- s2_bypart[match(unname(PARTS), s2_bypart$outcome), ]
s2_bypart$row <- s2_bypart$outcome

# --- D. Clusters rebuilt from raw items, for comparisons between clusters ---
# Study 2's clusters, built as Study 1 built them (raw items, plain means),
# exactly as section 7.6 of 01_main_analysis.Rmd builds them. GUARD: each must
# reproduce the correlation 01 exported before it is used.
s2_items <- list(
  hostile = c(paste0("exclusion_", 1:3), "degrad_1_R", "degrad_2", "degrad_3",
              "suffer_1", "suffer_2", "prisonvi_1_R", "prisonvi_2_R",
              "harsh_1", "harsh_2_R", "harsh_3", "revenge_1", "revenge_2",
              "revenge_3"),
  emotions = c("hate_1", "hate_2_R", "hate_3", "anger_1", "anger_2"),
  personality = shared_personality_items,
  crime = c("rates_1", "rates_2", "fear_1_R", "fear_2", "fear_3"))
stopifnot(all(unlist(s2_items) %in% names(s2)))
for (k in names(s2_items))
  s2[[paste0("cl_", k)]] <- rowMeans(s2[, s2_items[[k]]], na.rm = TRUE)
s2_rebuilt <- sapply(paste0("cl_", names(s2_items)),
                     function(v) cor(s2$punit_six, s2[[v]]))
stopifnot(all(abs(s2_rebuilt - s2_clu$r[match(unname(s1_clusters),
                                              s2_clu$cluster)]) < 1e-10))
```

# 5. The two studies compared

```{r compare}
# === CROSS-STUDY QUANTITIES ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: computes the handful of cross-study numbers the text
# reports, and writes every table the figures and the text draw on.
# PUNITIVENESS is the six components in both studies (Supplement S3 and
# Figures S1 to S3); the eight-item scale appears only in part A's second pair
# of rows, the comparison on the attitude items alone.
# PREREG: NOT REGISTERED (cross-study comparisons were never registered).
# CONSUMES: sections 3 and 4.
S1_NAME <- "Study 1 (N = 496)"
S2_NAME <- "Study 2 (N = 948)"

# --- A. How closely the two orderings agree ---------------------------------
# Spearman's rank correlation between the two studies' sixteen correlations on
# the six components: 1 would mean the same ordering exactly.
m16 <- merge(s1_con[, c("construct", "r")], s2_con[, c("construct", "r")],
             by = "construct", suffixes = c("_s1", "_s2"))
rho16 <- cor(m16$r_s1, m16$r_s2, method = "spearman")
# On the eight-item scale, which contains no sentencing data, how far apart are
# the two studies' correlations for the same twelve constructs?
m12 <- merge(s1_eight[, c("construct", "r")], s2_eight[, c("construct", "r")],
             by = "construct", suffixes = c("_s1", "_s2"))
agreement <- data.frame(
  quantity = c("Spearman rho, 16 constructs, six components",
               "Constructs larger in Study 2, six components (of 16)",
               "Largest absolute difference, 12 shared constructs, eight-item scale",
               "Constructs larger in Study 2, eight-item scale (of 12)"),
  value = c(rho16, sum(m16$r_s2 >= m16$r_s1),
            max(abs(m12$r_s2 - m12$r_s1)), sum(m12$r_s2 >= m12$r_s1)))
write.csv(agreement, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "two_study_agreement.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(agreement, digits = 3, caption = "How closely the two studies agree")

# --- B. Is crime concerns the lowest cluster, by test? ---------------------
# Each cluster against crime concerns, as Study 1 tested it, plus the top pair
# (hostile aggression against emotions). One-sided and two-sided p are both
# reported; Study 1's manuscript used two-sided.
gap_rows <- function(data, punit, host, emo, pers, crime, study) {
  rbind(
    cbind(study = study, comparison = "Hostile aggression vs crime concerns",
          two_steiger(data, punit, host, crime)),
    cbind(study = study, comparison = "Emotions vs crime concerns",
          two_steiger(data, punit, emo, crime)),
    cbind(study = study, comparison = "Personality and ideology vs crime concerns",
          two_steiger(data, punit, pers, crime)),
    cbind(study = study, comparison = "Hostile aggression vs emotions",
          two_steiger(data, punit, host, emo)))
}
cluster_gaps <- rbind(
  gap_rows(s1, "punit_six", "hostile_agg", "emotions_agg",
           "personality_agg", "crime_concerns_agg", S1_NAME),
  gap_rows(s2, "punit_six", "cl_hostile", "cl_emotions",
           "cl_personality", "cl_crime", S2_NAME))
# GUARDS. Study 1's three rows against crime concerns are the ones section 3c.2
# computed with its own two-sided call (h2: difference, Zou interval and Z), so
# the two routes agree. (Study 1's published-index rows were checked against
# its export in sections 3 and 3c.) Study 1's hostile-versus-emotions row is the
# verified six-component value, .068 [.019, .118], two-sided p = .006. Study
# 2's hostile-versus-crime row equals the top rung of 01's ladder
# (DS_tautology_ladder), which is on the six components.
for (f in c("diff", "diff_lower", "diff_upper", "z"))
  stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(cluster_gaps[[f]][1:3], h2[[f]][1:3], tolerance = 1e-10)))
stopifnot(round(cluster_gaps$diff[4], 3) == 0.068,
          round(cluster_gaps$diff_lower[4], 3) == 0.019,
          round(cluster_gaps$diff_upper[4], 3) == 0.118,
          round(cluster_gaps$p_two_sided[4], 3) == 0.006,
          isTRUE(all.equal(cluster_gaps$diff[5], s2_ladder$diff[1], tolerance = 1e-10)),
          isTRUE(all.equal(cluster_gaps$z[5], s2_ladder$z[1], tolerance = 1e-10)))
write.csv(cluster_gaps, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "two_study_cluster_tests.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(cluster_gaps[, c("study", "comparison", "diff", "diff_lower",
                              "diff_upper", "z", "p_two_sided")], digits = 4,
             caption = "Comparisons between clusters, both studies")

# --- C. The long tables the figures draw ----------------------------------
stack <- function(a, b, key) {
  a$study <- S1_NAME; b$study <- S2_NAME
  cols <- c("study", key, "r", "ci_lower", "ci_upper")
  rbind(a[, cols], b[, cols])
}
two_con <- stack(s1_con, s2_con, "construct")
two_clu <- stack(s1_clu, s2_clu, "cluster")
adv_cols <- c("diff", "diff_lower", "diff_upper", "z")
two_adv <- rbind(
  data.frame(study = S1_NAME, panel = "levels", row = s1_ladder$row, s1_ladder[, adv_cols]),
  data.frame(study = S2_NAME, panel = "levels", row = s2_ladder$row, s2_ladder[, adv_cols]),
  data.frame(study = S1_NAME, panel = "parts",  row = s1_bypart$row, s1_bypart[, adv_cols]),
  data.frame(study = S2_NAME, panel = "parts",  row = s2_bypart$row, s2_bypart[, adv_cols]))
clusters_out <- rbind(two_clu, data.frame(
  study = S1_NAME, cluster = "Personality and ideology (21 shared items)",
  r = s1_pers_shared$r, ci_lower = s1_pers_shared$ci_lower,
  ci_upper = s1_pers_shared$ci_upper))
write.csv(two_con, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "two_study_constructs.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(clusters_out, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "two_study_clusters.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(two_adv, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "two_study_hostility_advantage.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(clusters_out, digits = 3, caption = "The clusters, both studies")
knitr::kable(two_adv, digits = 3, caption = "The hostility advantage, both studies")
```

# 6. The sentencing decision in both studies

```{r sentences}
# === THE SENTENCE, BOTH STUDIES ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: describes each study's sentencing decisions on the same
# terms. Both studies gave the same instruction: "Most sentences given by judges
# for similar charges range from 20 to 30 years." Sentences are compared with
# the midpoint of that range, 25 years, as Study 1's manuscript did.
sent <- rbind(
  data.frame(study = S1_NAME, years = s1$Sentence_1),
  data.frame(study = S2_NAME, years = s2$Sentence1))
sent <- sent[!is.na(sent$years), ]
describe_sentences <- function(x) {
  top6 <- sort(table(x), decreasing = TRUE)[1:6]
  m <- mean(x); s <- sd(x)
  tt <- t.test(x, mu = 25)
  # Skew defined exactly as section 6.2 of 01_main_analysis.Rmd defines it: the
  # third central moment over the cube of the sample SD. (A population-moment
  # definition would differ in the fourth decimal, and the guard below would
  # rightly refuse it.)
  g1 <- mean((x - m)^3) / s^3
  data.frame(n = length(x), mean = m, sd = s, median = median(x),
             t_vs_25 = unname(tt$statistic), df = unname(tt$parameter),
             p_two_sided = tt$p.value, d_vs_25 = (m - 25) / s,
             share_below_20 = mean(x < 20),
             share_20_to_30 = mean(x >= 20 & x <= 30),
             share_above_30 = mean(x > 30),
             share_at_50 = mean(x == 50),
             six_modal_values = paste(names(top6), collapse = ", "),
             share_on_six = mean(x %in% as.numeric(names(top6))),
             skew = g1)
}
sent_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(sent$years, sent$study),
                                      describe_sentences))
sent_summary <- cbind(study = rownames(sent_summary), sent_summary)
rownames(sent_summary) <- NULL

# GUARDS, Study 1, against its manuscript: t(495) = 18.14, d = 0.81, 32.3% at 50,
# 86% on six values. The skew is not printed in the manuscript (which calls the
# distribution right-skewed; it is left-skewed), so it is not guarded here.
s1r <- sent_summary[sent_summary$study == S1_NAME, ]
stopifnot(abs(s1r$t_vs_25 - 18.14) < .005, abs(round(s1r$d_vs_25, 2) - .81) < 1e-9,
          abs(round(100 * s1r$share_at_50, 1) - 32.3) < 1e-9,
          abs(round(100 * s1r$share_on_six) - 86) < 1e-9)
# GUARDS, Study 2, against 01_main_analysis.Rmd's exports.
s2r <- sent_summary[sent_summary$study == S2_NAME, ]
s2desc <- read_s2("descriptives"); s2desc <- s2desc[s2desc$variable == "Sentence1", ]
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(s2r$mean, s2desc$mean, tolerance = 1e-10)),
          isTRUE(all.equal(s2r$sd, s2desc$sd, tolerance = 1e-10)),
          isTRUE(all.equal(s2r$skew, s2desc$skew, tolerance = 1e-8)),
          isTRUE(all.equal(s2r$share_at_50, read_s2("sentence_ceiling_share")$prop,
                           tolerance = 1e-10)),
          isTRUE(all.equal(s2r$share_on_six, read_s2("sentence_modal_share")$prop,
                           tolerance = 1e-10)))

# Is the ceiling more crowded in Study 2? A two-sample test of proportions with
# the 95% interval for the difference (Study 2 minus Study 1).
k  <- c(sum(s2$Sentence1 == 50, na.rm = TRUE), sum(s1$Sentence_1 == 50, na.rm = TRUE))
nn <- c(sum(!is.na(s2$Sentence1)), sum(!is.na(s1$Sentence_1)))
pt <- prop.test(k, nn, correct = FALSE)
sent_summary$ceiling_diff_s2_minus_s1 <- unname(pt$estimate[1] - pt$estimate[2])
sent_summary$ceiling_diff_lower <- pt$conf.int[1]
sent_summary$ceiling_diff_upper <- pt$conf.int[2]
sent_summary$ceiling_diff_p <- pt$p.value
write.csv(sent_summary, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "two_study_sentences.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(t(sent_summary[, -1]), digits = 3, col.names = sent_summary$study,
             caption = "The sentencing decision, both studies")
```

# 7. The figures

```{r figure_style}
# === ONE STYLE FOR ALL OF THE PAPER'S FIGURES ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: sets the look every figure shares and names the files.
#
# GRAYSCALE. The figures print in grays only, so they read the same in a printed
# journal, on screen, and to a reader who cannot tell colours apart. Where two
# studies sit side by side, Study 1 is the lighter gray and Study 2 the darker,
# and a legend names both. Study 1's two correlation matrices (fig2 and fig4)
# are drawn here too, on the six components, in the same grays (they replace
# Study 1's own colour versions).
# THE SHADES were checked with the data-visualization palette validator: each is
# visibly darker than the one before, and the lightest still stands apart from
# the white page.
S1_FILL <- "#b0b0b0"   # Study 1, and any lighter series
S2_FILL <- "#404040"   # Study 2, and any darker series
VIOLIN  <- "#d9d9d9"   # violin bodies, light so the points and means show
POINTS  <- "#595959"   # individual participants (jittered)
INK  <- "#000000"; INK2 <- "#404040"; GRID <- "#e6e6e6"; BAND <- "#efefef"
STUDY_FILL <- setNames(c(S1_FILL, S2_FILL), c(S1_NAME, S2_NAME))
# Figures are drawn at the width they will print (5.8 inches), so the type sizes
# set here are the sizes a reader sees. Journal figures carry no title inside
# the image; the caption in the manuscript is the title.
FIG_W <- 5.8
theme_paper <- function() {
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9.5, base_family = "sans") +
    theme(text = element_text(colour = INK),
          axis.text = element_text(colour = INK2),
          axis.title = element_text(colour = INK2),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          legend.position = "top", legend.title = element_blank(),
          legend.justification = "center",
          legend.key.size = unit(0.8, "lines"),
          plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10, hjust = 0),
          plot.title.position = "plot")
}
theme_hbar <- function() theme_paper() +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = GRID, linewidth = 0.3),
        axis.text.y = element_text(colour = INK))
theme_vbar <- function() theme_paper() +
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = GRID, linewidth = 0.3),
        axis.text.x = element_text(colour = INK))
# Correlations and differences print without the leading zero, with a true minus.
axis_r <- function(x) sub("^-", "−", sub("^(-?)0\\.", "\\1.", sprintf("%.1f", x)))
lab_r  <- expression(paste("Correlation with punitiveness (", italic(r), ") and 95% CI"))
lab_dr <- expression(paste("Hostility minus crime concerns (difference in ",
                           italic(r), ") and 95% CI"))

# WHERE THE FIGURES GO. Every figure is written to this document's output folder
# as PNG and PDF, and the PNG is copied to the manuscript's figure folder for
# the paper's figures, which the Word draft embeds.
DOCS_PAPER <- file.path("..", "..", "Docs", "Writing", "figures", "paper")
dir.create(DOCS_PAPER, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
# THE OVERLEAF VERSION of the manuscript uses the PDF of each figure (vector
# graphics, sharp at any size). Each PDF is copied into that project's figures
# folder, so the Overleaf project always carries the figures this knit drew.
OVERLEAF_FIG <- file.path("..", "..", "Docs", "Writing", "overleaf",
                          "retribution-results", "figures")
dir.create(OVERLEAF_FIG, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
# The Supplement has its own Overleaf project, whose figures folder must carry
# the same PDFs: every paper figure's PDF is copied there too, so the two
# projects can never show different versions of a figure (the Supplement uses
# fig5, fig6, fig7, fig9, fig12 and fig14; a copy of the others is harmless).
OVERLEAF_SUPP_FIG <- file.path("..", "..", "Docs", "Writing", "overleaf",
                               "retribution-supplement", "figures")
dir.create(OVERLEAF_SUPP_FIG, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
# Earlier versions of this document wrote three colour figures under other
# names. They are this document's own outputs; removing them from its output
# folder keeps only the current set there. (Copies in the manuscript's
# figures/study2 folder are left alone.)
unlink(file.path(OUT_FIGURES, paste0(c("fig_sentences_both_studies",
                                       "fig_correlates_both_studies",
                                       "fig_hostility_advantage_both_studies"),
                                     rep(c(".png", ".pdf"), each = 3))))
# THE PDF DEVICE. R's default pdf() device cannot encode a Greek letter such as
# the kappa in Figure 14 (it prints a period instead), draws every hyphen as a
# long minus sign, and does not embed its fonts, which journal PDF checks flag.
# On a Mac the figures are drawn with the system's own quartz PDF device, which
# has none of these faults and spaces letters evenly. Elsewhere cairo_pdf() is
# used: it too prints the kappa and real hyphens and embeds its fonts, though it
# rounds each letter's width, so letter spacing is slightly uneven.
PDF_DEVICE <- if (capabilities("aqua")) {
  function(filename, width, height, bg = "white", ...)
    grDevices::quartz(type = "pdf", file = filename, width = width, height = height, bg = bg,
                      title = tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(filename)))
} else {
  grDevices::cairo_pdf
}
# save_fig(): writes the figure as PNG and PDF to this document's output folder
# and, for a figure in the paper (paper = TRUE, the default), copies the PNG to
# the manuscript's figure folder and the PDF to the Overleaf figure folder. A
# figure that is no longer in the paper (fig3) is written with paper = FALSE,
# so a knit never puts it back in the manuscript's folders. (A copy left there
# by an earlier knit is not deleted here: the drafts decide which figures they
# embed, and removing a file a draft still names would break its build.)
save_fig <- function(p, name, h, paper = TRUE) {
  png_path <- file.path(OUT_FIGURES, paste0(name, ".png"))
  ggsave(png_path, p, width = FIG_W, height = h, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
  pdf_path <- file.path(OUT_FIGURES, paste0(name, ".pdf"))
  ggsave(pdf_path, p, width = FIG_W, height = h, bg = "white", device = PDF_DEVICE)
  if (paper) {
    stopifnot(file.copy(png_path, file.path(DOCS_PAPER, basename(png_path)), overwrite = TRUE),
              file.copy(pdf_path, file.path(OVERLEAF_FIG, basename(pdf_path)), overwrite = TRUE),
              file.copy(pdf_path, file.path(OVERLEAF_SUPP_FIG, basename(pdf_path)), overwrite = TRUE))
    PAPER_FIGS <<- c(PAPER_FIGS, name)
  }
  invisible(NULL)
}
# The paper figures this knit writes, listed at the end (section 10).
PAPER_FIGS <- character(0)
# A 95% interval for a mean.
mean_ci <- function(x) {
  tt <- t.test(x)
  data.frame(mean = mean(x), lower = tt$conf.int[1], upper = tt$conf.int[2])
}

# VIOLIN WITH JITTERED POINTS, used by fig5 and fig13. The violin is the shape
# of the sentences (wider where more participants chose that sentence). Each
# small point is one participant, spread sideways at random so that people who
# chose the same sentence do not sit on top of one another; the spread is
# sideways only, so every point stays at the sentence the participant chose.
# The seed fixes the random spread, so every knit draws the same figure. The
# large black point is the mean and the black bar its 95% interval. The shaded
# band is the 20-to-30-year range the instructions gave; the dashed line is its
# 25-year midpoint.
violin_sentences <- function(long, stats) {
  ggplot(long, aes(x = group, y = years)) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = 20, ymax = 30,
             fill = BAND, colour = NA) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 25, linetype = "dashed", colour = INK2, linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_violin(fill = VIOLIN, colour = "#7a7a7a", linewidth = 0.35, width = 0.85,
                adjust = 1.4, trim = TRUE) +
    geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.2, height = 0, seed = 1),
               size = 0.7, alpha = 0.45, colour = POINTS, stroke = 0) +
    geom_errorbar(data = stats, aes(x = group, ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
                  inherit.aes = FALSE, width = 0.12, linewidth = 0.6, colour = INK) +
    geom_point(data = stats, aes(x = group, y = mean), inherit.aes = FALSE,
               size = 2.2, colour = INK) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 50, 10), limits = c(0, 50),
                       expand = expansion(add = 1)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Years in prison (50 = life)") +
    theme_vbar()
}
```

```{r corr_matrix_tools}
# === THE CORRELATION-MATRIX FIGURES (fig2 AND fig4): SHARED DRAWING FUNCTION ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: defines corr_matrix_fig(), which draws the correlations
# among a set of Study 1 measures as a triangle of gray cells, each with its r
# printed in it.
# DESIGN. Only the cells below the diagonal are drawn: the matrix is symmetric,
# so the upper triangle would repeat them, and the diagonal is 1 by definition.
# Punitiveness is the first measure, so the first column is every measure's
# correlation with punitiveness, the quantity the paper's H1 and H2 are about.
# The shade runs from a very light gray (r = 0, still visible against the white
# page) to near black (r = 1): one ramp, because every correlation here is
# positive (guarded below; a negative r would need a second ramp, and the knit
# stops rather than draw it misleadingly). The number in each cell carries the
# exact value, so the figure has no colour key. Each number is printed in
# white or black, whichever contrasts more with its own cell; the guard below
# confirms every number keeps a contrast of at least 4.5 to 1 (the WCAG level
# for normal text).
# CONSUMES: s1 with punit_six (section 3.0); theme_paper(), INK (figure_style).
MAT_LOW <- "#f0f0f0"; MAT_HIGH <- "#1a1a1a"
# Relative luminance of a gray (WCAG 2 definition), for the text contrast.
gray_lum <- function(hex) {
  v <- grDevices::col2rgb(hex)[1, ] / 255
  ifelse(v <= 0.03928, v / 12.92, ((v + 0.055) / 1.055)^2.4)
}
corr_matrix_fig <- function(vars, labels, text_size, x_angle = 0, wrap = 12) {
  stopifnot(length(vars) == length(labels), all(vars %in% names(s1)), !anyNA(s1[, vars]))
  R <- cor(s1[, vars])
  k <- length(vars)
  cells <- expand.grid(i = seq_len(k), j = seq_len(k))
  cells <- cells[cells$i > cells$j, ]          # below the diagonal: row i, column j
  cells$r <- R[cbind(cells$i, cells$j)]
  # GUARD: every correlation drawn is positive, so the one-ramp shading is
  # honest (see DESIGN above).
  stopifnot(all(cells$r > 0))
  # The gray each cell will be drawn in: the same palette scale_fill_gradient()
  # uses below (interpolated in Lab space between the two ends; with limits 0
  # to 1, r needs no rescaling). The text takes whichever of white and black
  # contrasts more with that gray. GUARD: at least 4.5 to 1 in every cell.
  lum <- gray_lum(scales::seq_gradient_pal(MAT_LOW, MAT_HIGH, "Lab")(cells$r))
  c_white <- 1.05 / (lum + 0.05); c_black <- (lum + 0.05) / 0.05
  cells$white_text <- c_white > c_black
  stopifnot(all(pmax(c_white, c_black) >= 4.5))
  # Rows run top to bottom in the measures' order, columns left to right.
  cells$row <- factor(labels[cells$i], levels = rev(labels))
  cells$col <- factor(labels[cells$j], levels = labels)
  cells$lab <- sub("^0\\.", ".", sprintf("%.2f", cells$r))
  x_lab <- if (x_angle == 0) function(x) vapply(x, function(s)
    paste(strwrap(s, width = wrap), collapse = "\n"), character(1)) else waiver()
  p <- ggplot(cells, aes(x = col, y = row, fill = r)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_text(aes(label = lab, colour = white_text), size = text_size,
              show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = MAT_LOW, high = MAT_HIGH, limits = c(0, 1), guide = "none") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = INK), guide = "none") +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = x_lab, drop = TRUE) +
    scale_y_discrete(drop = TRUE) +
    coord_fixed(clip = "off") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_paper() +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),
          axis.text.y = element_text(colour = INK, hjust = 1),
          axis.text.x = if (x_angle == 0) element_text(colour = INK, lineheight = 0.9) else
            element_text(colour = INK, angle = x_angle, hjust = 1, vjust = 1))
  list(plot = p, R = R)
}
```

## Figure 6: punitiveness and its correlates in both studies

```{r figure6_correlates, fig.width = 5.8, fig.height = 7.4}
# === FIGURE 6: THE CORRELATES AND THE CLUSTERS, BOTH STUDIES (BAR CHART) ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: Panel A: every construct both studies fielded, each
# study's correlation with punitiveness (the six components, in both studies)
# and its 95% interval. Panel B: the four clusters.
# PREREG: NOT REGISTERED (the paper's scoring; cross-study comparisons were
#         never registered).
# CONSUMES: two_con, two_clu (section 5); s1_con, s1_clu (section 3); STUDY_FILL,
#           theme_hbar(), lab_r, axis_r (figure style).
# GUARD: the row order factors cover every row (no construct or cluster lost).
# Rows are ORDERED BY STUDY 1 (its correlations on the six components, largest
# at the top), so a reader can see directly whether Study 2 keeps that order.
# Panel B shows Study 1's thirty-item
# personality cluster; the twenty-one-item version is in two_study_clusters.csv.
# position_dodge() places the FIRST level lowest; ordering the studies Study 2
# then Study 1 puts Study 1's bar on top in every row, as the legend reads.
bar_panel <- function(df, key, title) {
  df$study <- factor(df$study, levels = c(S2_NAME, S1_NAME))
  dodge <- position_dodge(width = 0.8)
  ggplot(df, aes(x = r, y = .data[[key]], fill = study)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.76, position = dodge) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = ci_lower, xmax = ci_upper), width = 0.25,
                  orientation = "y", linewidth = 0.35, colour = INK, position = dodge) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = INK2, linewidth = 0.4) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = STUDY_FILL, breaks = c(S1_NAME, S2_NAME)) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 0.8, 0.1), labels = axis_r) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 0.8)) +
    labs(x = lab_r, y = NULL, title = title) +
    theme_hbar()
}
# Study 1's order is the order of ITS correlations on the six components,
# largest at the top (the published order was on the published index, and a
# few adjacent rows swap places under the six components, e.g. hatred and
# social exclusion). order() puts the smallest first, which ggplot draws at the
# bottom.
two_con$construct <- factor(two_con$construct,
                            levels = s1_con$construct[order(s1_con$r)])
two_clu$cluster <- factor(two_clu$cluster, levels = s1_clu$cluster[order(s1_clu$r)])
stopifnot(!anyNA(two_con$construct), !anyNA(two_clu$cluster))
fig6 <- bar_panel(two_con, "construct", "A. Each construct") /
  (bar_panel(two_clu, "cluster", "B. The four clusters") +
     theme(legend.position = "none")) +
  plot_layout(heights = c(16, 4.6))
save_fig(fig6, "fig6_correlates_both_studies", 7.4)
fig6
```

```{r figure7_advantage, fig.width = 5.8, fig.height = 5.2}
# === FIGURE 7: HOW MUCH MORE CLOSELY PUNITIVENESS TRACKS HOSTILITY (BAR CHART) ===
# PREREG: NOT REGISTERED as scored (see below). CONSUMES: two_adv (section 5),
# LEVELS and PARTS (section 3), whose values sections 3 and 4 guarded.
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: the difference between the two correlations (hostile aggression minus crime
# concerns) with its 95% interval. Panel A: the three levels of the sensitivity
# analysis. Panel B: the all-six-construct comparison on each part of
# punitiveness separately. Panel A's punitiveness is the six components in both
# studies (NOT REGISTERED); Panel B's rows are single parts, so no weighting
# enters. INTERVALS are Zou's (2007), computed identically in both studies.
# Study 1's Table S1 reports BCa bootstrap intervals for the three levels
# (S1P_tableS1_strictness, section 3c.2); those are close to these but are not
# the same interval.
adv_panel <- function(df, title) {
  df$study <- factor(df$study, levels = c(S2_NAME, S1_NAME))
  dodge <- position_dodge(width = 0.8)
  ggplot(df, aes(x = diff, y = row, fill = study)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.76, position = dodge) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = diff_lower, xmax = diff_upper), width = 0.25,
                  orientation = "y", linewidth = 0.35, colour = INK, position = dodge) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = INK2, linewidth = 0.4) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = STUDY_FILL, breaks = c(S1_NAME, S2_NAME)) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 0.4, 0.1), labels = axis_r) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-0.05, 0.45)) +
    labs(x = lab_dr, y = NULL, title = title) +
    theme_hbar()
}
lev_df  <- two_adv[two_adv$panel == "levels", ]
lev_df$row <- factor(lev_df$row, levels = rev(LEVELS))
part_df <- two_adv[two_adv$panel == "parts", ]
part_df$row <- factor(part_df$row, levels = rev(unname(PARTS)))
fig7 <- adv_panel(lev_df, "A. Three levels of strictness") /
  (adv_panel(part_df, "B. Each component of punitiveness") +
     theme(legend.position = "none")) +
  plot_layout(heights = c(3, 6))
save_fig(fig7, "fig7_hostility_advantage_both_studies", 5.2)
fig7
```

# 8. Study 2's own figures (Results, Part 2)

These six figures show Study 2 alone, for Part 2 of its Results ("What people
mean by retribution"). They use the same grayscale style as the figures above
and the same checks: every number that also exists in `01_main_analysis.Rmd`'s
exports is compared with it, and the knit stops if any disagrees.

```{r study2_paper_tools}
# === SHARED PIECES FOR THE STUDY 2 FIGURES ===
# fmt_r prints a correlation without the leading zero and with a true minus
# sign; a correlation smaller than .01 in size gets three decimals (.007), since
# two would misstate it as .00 or .01.
fmt_r <- function(x) {
  dg <- ifelse(abs(x) < 0.01, 3, 2)
  s <- vapply(seq_along(x), function(i) formatC(x[i], format = "f", digits = dg[i]),
              character(1))
  sub("^-", "−", sub("^(-?)0\\.", "\\1.", s))
}
# A Pearson correlation with its Fisher-z 95% interval, as cor.test() gives it.
cor_ci2 <- function(x, y) {
  tt <- cor.test(x, y)
  data.frame(r = unname(tt$estimate), lower = tt$conf.int[1], upper = tt$conf.int[2])
}
# GUARD: two numbers must agree to within a tolerance, or the knit stops and
# names the check that failed.
same <- function(a, b, what, tol = 1e-8) {
  if (!isTRUE(all.equal(as.numeric(a), as.numeric(b), tolerance = tol)))
    stop("Guard failed: ", what)
  invisible(TRUE)
}
# Four evenly spaced grays for stacked bars, darkest first (validated as an
# ordered ramp: each step visibly darker than the next, the lightest still
# distinct from the white page).
RAMP4 <- c("#1a1a1a", "#4f4f4f", "#808080", "#b0b0b0")
# Horizontal bars with a 95% interval and the value printed past the interval.
# `fill` names the column that sets each bar's gray; dodge > 0 puts two bars in
# each row. position_dodge() places the first factor level lowest, so callers
# order the levels to put the series named first in the legend on top.
bars_r <- function(df, y, fill, fills, xlim, xbreaks, xlab, dodge = 0,
                   legend_breaks = names(fills)) {
  pos <- if (dodge > 0) position_dodge(width = dodge) else position_identity()
  ggplot(df, aes(x = r, y = .data[[y]], fill = .data[[fill]])) +
    geom_col(width = if (dodge > 0) dodge * 0.95 else 0.65, position = pos) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper), width = 0.25, orientation = "y",
                  linewidth = 0.35, colour = INK, position = pos) +
    geom_text(aes(x = pmax(upper, 0) + 0.012, label = fmt_r(r)), hjust = 0,
              size = 2.6, colour = INK, position = pos, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = INK2, linewidth = 0.4) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = fills, breaks = legend_breaks) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = xbreaks, labels = axis_r) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = xlim, clip = "off") +
    labs(x = xlab, y = NULL) +
    theme_hbar()
}
# Violins of 1-to-7 scores: the shape of everyone's answers, each participant as
# a point jittered sideways only (so it stays at its score; the seed fixes the
# jitter), and the mean with its 95% interval in black. The dashed line is the
# neutral midpoint.
violins_1to7 <- function(long, stats, levels) {
  long$measure <- factor(long$measure, levels = levels)
  stats$measure <- factor(stats$measure, levels = levels)
  ggplot(long, aes(x = measure, y = score)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 4, linetype = "dashed", colour = INK2, linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_violin(fill = VIOLIN, colour = "#7a7a7a", linewidth = 0.35, width = 0.85,
                scale = "width", adjust = 1.2, trim = TRUE) +
    geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.2, height = 0, seed = 1),
               size = 0.6, alpha = 0.35, colour = POINTS, stroke = 0) +
    geom_errorbar(data = stats, aes(x = measure, ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
                  inherit.aes = FALSE, width = 0.12, linewidth = 0.6, colour = INK) +
    geom_point(data = stats, aes(x = measure, y = mean), inherit.aes = FALSE,
               size = 2.2, colour = INK) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = 1:7, limits = c(1, 7),
                       labels = c("1 Strongly\ndisagree", "2", "3", "4 Neutral", "5",
                                  "6", "7 Strongly\nagree")) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_vbar() + theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7.5, lineheight = 0.9))
}
```

## The paper's scorings of Study 2

```{r study2_paper_scorings}
# === THE PAPER'S SCORINGS OF STUDY 2 ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: builds s2p, a copy of the scored data with the paper's
# scores added, each built exactly as section 9.19 of 01_main_analysis.Rmd
# builds it and checked against what 9.19 exported. fig10 to fig13, fig15 and
# fig18 read from s2p; every other figure reads s2 and is unchanged.
#
# THE PAPER'S SCORINGS (none registered; the Method lists them, and the
# Supplement lists each as a departure), as settled on 27 September 2026:
#   desert_theory       "desert theory": the mean of Retribution_1 to _5, the
#                       five retribution items (alpha .913, M 5.60). The
#                       registered desert score is items 1 to 4.
#   just_deserts_paper  the paper's "just deserts": the plain mean of desert
#                       theory and the proportionality principle item (both 1
#                       to 7, so the mean stays on the 1-to-7 scale and can be
#                       compared with revenge's mean). The registered
#                       composite, s2$just_deserts, is "just deserts
#                       (registered)" and stays in s2p unchanged.
#   punit_parts6        punitiveness, the six components weighted equally
#                       (s2$punit_six, section 4.0), under the variable name
#                       01's contrast exports use for it.
#   punit_parts5z       punitiveness, the five attitude components each
#                       standardized (s2$punit_five_z), used wherever the
#                       sentence or the sentencing ratio is on the other side.
# Revenge (four items) and the hostile aggression cluster are used as
# registered, so s2p carries them unchanged from s2.
PAPER_NEEDED <- c("PAPER_reliability", "PAPER_H6", "PAPER_H6_cors", "PAPER_H9",
                  "PAPER_H10_cors", "PAPER_goals_by_limits", "PAPER_ratio_cors",
                  "PAPER_ratio_continuous", "PAPER_contrasts_rank",
                  "PAPER_contrasts_vs_deter_incap", "PAPER_H1",
                  "PAPER_H12_shares_vs_deter_incap", "PAPER_person_scores",
                  "PAPER_JD_parts", "PAPER_JD_H9", "PAPER_JD_H10_cors")
PAPER_MISSING <- PAPER_NEEDED[!file.exists(file.path(S2_TABLES,
                                                     paste0(PAPER_NEEDED, ".csv")))]
if (length(PAPER_MISSING)) stop("Knit 01_main_analysis.Rmd first (the PAPER_ files ",
                                "come from its section 9.19). Missing: ",
                                paste(PAPER_MISSING, collapse = ", "))

# Every item was required, so no row is missing an item; checked here because
# a missing item would silently turn a row mean into a mean of fewer items.
RET_ITEMS <- paste0("Retribution_", 1:5)
stopifnot(!anyNA(s2[, RET_ITEMS]), !anyNA(s2$proportionality_principle),
          all(s2$proportionality_principle %in% 1:7))
s2p <- s2
s2p$desert_theory      <- rowMeans(s2[, RET_ITEMS])
s2p$just_deserts_paper <- (s2p$desert_theory + s2$proportionality_principle) / 2
s2p$punit_parts6       <- s2$punit_six
s2p$punit_parts5z      <- s2$punit_five_z

# GUARDS against section 9.19's exports:
#   desert theory's mean and SD (PAPER_reliability's "Desert theory (paper)"
#   row) and its value for every participant (PAPER_person_scores);
#   the paper's just deserts for every participant (PAPER_person_scores) and
#   its mean (PAPER_JD_parts, whole sample: 5.66);
#   the six-component score's mean and SD (PAPER_reliability); and
#   the retributivists' and the other participants' means on the hostile
#   aggression cluster (PAPER_contrasts_rank), which confirm that 9.19 used the
#   registered cluster that s2 carries.
prel <- read_s2("PAPER_reliability")
p_ret <- prel[grepl("^Desert theory \\(paper\\)", prel$score), ]
p_six <- prel[grepl("^Punitiveness \\(six components\\)", prel$score), ]
stopifnot(nrow(p_ret) == 1, nrow(p_six) == 1, p_ret$k == 5, p_six$k == 6)
same(mean(s2p$desert_theory), p_ret$M, "desert theory, mean")
same(sd(s2p$desert_theory), p_ret$SD, "desert theory, SD")
same(s2p$desert_theory, ps2$desert_theory, "desert theory, every participant")
same(s2p$just_deserts_paper, ps2$just_deserts, "just deserts (paper), every participant")
pjd <- read_s2("PAPER_JD_parts")
pjd_all <- pjd[pjd$sample == "Whole sample", ]
stopifnot(nrow(pjd_all) == 1)
same(mean(s2p$just_deserts_paper), pjd_all$M_just_deserts, "just deserts (paper), mean")
same(mean(s2p$punit_parts6), p_six$M, "six components, mean", tol = 1e-6)
same(sd(s2p$punit_parts6), p_six$SD, "six components, SD")
pcr <- read_s2("PAPER_contrasts_rank")
p_hag <- pcr[pcr$outcome == "Hostile-aggression cluster (z)", ]
stopifnot(nrow(p_hag) == 1, p_hag$variable == "hostile_agg")
RET_P <- s2$grp_rank == "Retributivist"
stopifnot(!anyNA(RET_P), sum(RET_P) == 371)
same(mean(s2p$hostile_agg[RET_P]), p_hag$M1, "cluster, retributivists")
same(mean(s2p$hostile_agg[!RET_P]), p_hag$M2, "cluster, the others")
cat(sprintf(paste("Desert theory M = %.2f; just deserts (paper) M = %.2f;",
                  "revenge (four items) M = %.2f.\n"),
            mean(s2p$desert_theory), mean(s2p$just_deserts_paper), mean(s2p$revenge)))
```

## Figure 18: the twelve H1 correlations in Study 2

```{r figure18_study2_correlates, fig.width = 5.8, fig.height = 3.6}
# === FIGURE 18: EACH REGISTERED CORRELATE WITH PUNITIVENESS (H1) ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: plots each of the twelve registered correlates'
# correlation with punitiveness, the six components, with its 95% interval, as
# 01_main_analysis.Rmd exported them (PAPER_H1, section 9.19B), shaded by the
# H2 cluster each correlate belongs to. It is the paper version of the talk
# slide s2_02, on the paper's punitiveness measure. Each correlation is
# recomputed from the scored data as a check.
# PREREG: H1 is registered on the eight-item scale (Supplement); this is the
#         same family on the paper's score, NOT REGISTERED.
ph1 <- read_s2("PAPER_H1")
H1_VARS <- c("Harsh prison conditions" = "harsh", "Hatred" = "hatred",
             "Social exclusion" = "exclusion", "Infliction of suffering" = "suffering",
             "Due-process permissiveness" = "dueprocess", "Revenge" = "revenge",
             "Degradation" = "degradation", "Anger" = "anger",
             "Perceived crime rates" = "crimerates",
             "Tolerance of prison violence" = "prisonviol",
             "Convicting on uncertain evidence" = "uncertain", "Fear of crime" = "fear")
stopifnot(setequal(ph1$y, names(H1_VARS)), nrow(ph1) == 12)
# The registered H2 clusters (prereg 2.1): hostile aggression has five members
# and crime concerns two; the other five correlates belong to neither.
H1_HOSTILE <- c("hatred", "revenge", "degradation", "suffering", "prisonviol")
H1_CRIME   <- c("crimerates", "fear")
f18 <- data.frame(measure = ph1$y, r = ph1$r, lower = ph1$ci_lower, upper = ph1$ci_upper,
                  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
f18$var <- unname(H1_VARS[f18$measure])
for (i in seq_len(nrow(f18)))
  same(cor(s2p$punit_parts6, s2p[[f18$var[i]]]), f18$r[i], paste("r,", f18$measure[i]))
CL18 <- c("Hostile aggression cluster", "Crime concerns cluster", "Neither cluster")
f18$cluster <- ifelse(f18$var %in% H1_HOSTILE, CL18[1], ifelse(f18$var %in% H1_CRIME, CL18[2], CL18[3]))
f18$measure <- factor(f18$measure, levels = f18$measure[order(f18$r)])
fig18 <- bars_r(f18, "measure", "cluster",
                fills = setNames(c(S2_FILL, S1_FILL, "#7a7a7a"), CL18),
                xlim = c(0, 0.72), xbreaks = seq(0, 0.6, 0.2), xlab = lab_r,
                legend_breaks = CL18)
save_fig(fig18, "fig18_study2_correlates", 3.6)
fig18
```

## Figure 8: ranking the goals of punishment

```{r figure8_goals, fig.width = 5.8, fig.height = 2.4}
# === FIGURE 8: RANKING THE FOUR GOALS ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: draws the share of participants placing each goal 1st
# to 4th, from the exported rank matrix (goal_rank_matrix, registered). Since
# 27 September 2026 the figure is this ranking alone: the panel of the goal
# ratings (violins of each goal scale) was dropped, and the ratings are
# reported in the text and the Supplement. With one panel, the figure carries
# no panel letter or title inside the image.
# PREREG: the ranking is registered (prereg 5.5); descriptive, no test.
# CONSUMES: read_s2() (section 1); RAMP4, theme_hbar() (figure style).
rk <- read_s2("goal_rank_matrix")
rk$goal <- ifelse(grepl("retribution", rk$goal), "Retribution",
           ifelse(grepl("incapacitation", rk$goal), "Incapacitation",
           ifelse(grepl("deterrence", rk$goal), "Deterrence", "Rehabilitation")))
GOALS <- c("Retribution", "Incapacitation", "Deterrence", "Rehabilitation")
stopifnot(setequal(rk$goal, GOALS),
          all(rowSums(rk[, c("first", "second", "third", "fourth")]) == 948))
PLACES <- c(first = "1st", second = "2nd", third = "3rd", fourth = "4th")
rank_long <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(PLACES), function(p)
  data.frame(goal = rk$goal, place = PLACES[[p]], pct = 100 * rk[[p]] / 948)))
rank_long$place <- factor(rank_long$place, levels = unname(PLACES))
rank_long$goal <- factor(rank_long$goal, levels = rev(GOALS))
f8a <- ggplot(rank_long, aes(x = pct, y = goal, fill = place)) +
  # reverse = TRUE puts 1st place at the left of each bar; group = place keeps
  # the labels in the same stacking order as the bars.
  geom_col(width = 0.7, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.5,
           position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.0f%%", pct), group = place,
                colour = place %in% c("1st", "2nd", "3rd")),
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5, reverse = TRUE), size = 2.6,
            show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = INK), guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = setNames(RAMP4, unname(PLACES))) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.01))) +
  labs(x = "Participants", y = NULL) +
  theme_hbar() +
  # A right margin wide enough for the "100%" tick label, which would otherwise
  # be cut at the image's edge.
  theme(plot.margin = margin(5.5, 14, 5.5, 5.5))
fig8 <- f8a
```

```{r figure9_proportionality, fig.width = 5.8, fig.height = 2.6}
# === FIGURE 9: DISAGREE / NEUTRAL / AGREE ON THE THREE ITEMS (H4, H5) ===
ITEMS <- c(proportionality = "“Proportionate to the severity\nof the crime, no more and no less”",
           severity_1 = "“Greater than the\nseriousness of the crime”",
```

```{r figure10_retribution, fig.width = 5.8, fig.height = 1.6}
# === FIGURE 10: DESERT THEORY WITH THE PROPORTIONALITY PRINCIPLE AND WITH THE

# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: draws desert theory's correlation with the
# proportionality principle (.199) and with the severity index (.474), each
# with its 95% interval, as 01 exported them (PAPER_H6_cors, rows 1 and 2), and
# recomputes both from the scored data as a check. Since 27 September 2026 the
# figure shows these two bars only: the rows for the two single severity items
# and every punitiveness bar were dropped (punitiveness's correlations with the
# principle and the severity index, now on the six components, .038 and .588,
# are reported in the text from PAPER_H6).
# PREREG: H6 is registered on the registered desert score; this is the paper's
#         desert theory (Retribution_1 to _5), NOT REGISTERED as scored.
# CONSUMES: s2p (study2_paper_scorings); read_s2(), bars_r(), same().
h6c <- read_s2("PAPER_H6_cors"); h6s <- read_s2("PAPER_H6")
MEAS <- c("Proportionality principle", "Severity index")
MEAS_VAR <- c("proportionality_principle", "severity_index")
stopifnot(h6c$x[1] == "Desert theory", h6c$x[2] == "Desert theory",
          grepl("^Proportionality principle", h6c$y[1]), grepl("^Severity index", h6c$y[2]))
f10 <- data.frame(series = "Desert theory", measure = MEAS, r = h6c$r[1:2],
                  lower = h6c$ci_lower[1:2], upper = h6c$ci_upper[1:2])
same(f10$r, vapply(MEAS_VAR, function(v) cor(s2p$desert_theory, s2[[v]]), numeric(1)),
     "desert theory rows")
# GUARD: the two bars are the two correlations H6's test compares (PAPER_H6,
# desert theory row: r_jk with the severity index, r_jh with the principle).
p_dt <- h6s[h6s$pair == "Desert theory", ]
stopifnot(nrow(p_dt) == 1)
same(f10$r, c(p_dt$r_jh, p_dt$r_jk), "the two correlations H6 compares")
f10$measure <- factor(f10$measure, levels = rev(MEAS))
fig10 <- bars_r(f10, "measure", "series", fills = c(`Desert theory` = S2_FILL),
                xlim = c(0, 0.6), xbreaks = seq(0, 0.6, 0.2),
                xlab = expression(paste("Correlation with desert theory (", italic(r),
                                        ") and 95% CI"))) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
save_fig(fig10, "fig10_study2_desert_direction", 1.6)
fig10
```

## Figure 11: each goal against each limit

```{r figure11_limits, fig.width = 5.8, fig.height = 3.2}
# === FIGURE 11: GOALS AGAINST PARSIMONY AND AGAINST THE PROPORTIONALITY
# PRINCIPLE (PAPER_goals_by_limits, section 9.19) ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: each goal's correlation with the two limits, with 95%
# intervals, read from 01's export; desert theory's correlation with the
# principle is recomputed from the scored data as a check (GUARD, below).
# CONSUMES: s2p (study2_paper_scorings); read_s2(), same(), fmt_r().
# Retribution is desert theory (the five retribution items; its label in the
# figure is "Desert theory"); the limit of proportionality is the principle
# item, the paper's measure of it. Parsimony is its two items, scored so that
# agreement means accepting the limit. NOT REGISTERED (the paper's scoring).
gl <- read_s2("PAPER_goals_by_limits")
stopifnot(nrow(gl) == 12, setequal(gl$x, c("Desert theory", "Deterrence",
                                           "Incapacitation", "Rehabilitation")))
LIM <- c("Parsimony (2 items)" = "Parsimony (two items)",
         "Proportionality principle item alone" = "Proportionality principle")
gl$goal <- gl$x
same(gl$r[gl$goal == "Desert theory" & gl$y == "Proportionality principle item alone"],
     cor(s2p$desert_theory, s2$proportionality_principle),
     "desert theory x proportionality principle (H6)")
g11 <- gl[gl$y %in% names(LIM), ]
g11$limit <- factor(LIM[g11$y], levels = unname(LIM))
g11$goal <- factor(g11$goal, levels = c("Desert theory", "Deterrence", "Incapacitation",
                                        "Rehabilitation"))
stopifnot(nrow(g11) == 8, !anyNA(g11$limit), !anyNA(g11$goal))
DG <- position_dodge(width = 0.8)
fig11 <- ggplot(g11, aes(x = goal, y = r, fill = limit)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = INK2, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_col(width = 0.76, position = DG) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_lower, ymax = ci_upper), width = 0.2, linewidth = 0.35,
                colour = INK, position = DG) +
  geom_text(aes(y = ifelse(r >= 0, ci_upper + 0.02, ci_lower - 0.02),
                vjust = ifelse(r >= 0, 0, 1), label = fmt_r(r)),
            position = DG, size = 2.6, colour = INK) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = setNames(c(S2_FILL, S1_FILL), unname(LIM))) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-0.5, 0.3, 0.1), labels = axis_r) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-0.56, 0.34), clip = "off") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = expression(paste("Correlation with the limit (", italic(r), ") and 95% CI"))) +
  theme_vbar()
save_fig(fig11, "fig11_study2_goals_limits", 3.2)
fig11
```

## Figure 12: desert theory, just deserts and revenge

```{r figure12_revenge, fig.width = 5.8, fig.height = 5.4}
# === FIGURE 12: ENDORSEMENT (A) AND CORRELATION WITH PUNITIVENESS (B) ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: each panel shows four scores side by side, so the
# Supplement can set the registered H9 and H10 beside the paper's versions:
#   Desert theory              the five retribution items (paper);
#   Just deserts               the paper's just deserts: the mean of desert
#                              theory and the proportionality principle;
#   Just deserts (registered)  the registered composite (desert, items 1 to 4,
#                              with the registered proportionality component);
#   Revenge                    its four registered items.
# Panel A: each score's distribution, mean and 95% interval (1 to 7). Panel B:
# each score's correlation with punitiveness, the six components, for every
# row; the registered H10 test used the eight-item scale (H10_steiger), and the
# Supplement's text reports it there.
# PREREG: H9 and H10 are registered on the registered just-deserts score; the
#         desert-theory and paper just-deserts rows are NOT REGISTERED.
# CONSUMES: s2p (study2_paper_scorings); read_s2(), mean_ci(), cor_ci2(),
#           violins_1to7(), bars_r(), same().
ENDORSE <- c("Desert theory", "Just deserts", "Just deserts (registered)", "Revenge")
END_COL <- list(s2p$desert_theory, s2p$just_deserts_paper, s2$just_deserts, s2$revenge)
h9p <- read_s2("PAPER_H9"); h9 <- read_s2("H9_paired"); h9j <- read_s2("PAPER_JD_H9")
stopifnot(h9$var1[1] == "just_deserts", h9$var2[1] == "revenge", h9p$var2 == "revenge",
          h9j$comparison[1] == "Just deserts vs revenge", h9j$var2[1] == "revenge")
endorse <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(ENDORSE), function(i)
  cbind(measure = ENDORSE[i], mean_ci(END_COL[[i]]))))
# GUARDS: each mean is the one its H9 test compared. Desert theory and revenge
# against PAPER_H9; the paper's just deserts against PAPER_JD_H9 (5.66 against
# revenge's 4.14); the registered just deserts and revenge against the
# registered H9_paired.
same(endorse$mean[1], h9p$M1, "desert theory mean"); same(endorse$mean[4], h9p$M2, "revenge mean")
same(endorse$mean[2], h9j$M1[1], "just deserts (paper) mean")
same(endorse$mean[4], h9j$M2[1], "revenge mean, paper's just-deserts H9")
same(endorse$mean[3], h9$M1[1], "just deserts (registered) mean")
same(endorse$mean[4], h9$M2[1], "revenge mean, registered H9")
endorse_long <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(ENDORSE), function(i)
  data.frame(measure = ENDORSE[i], score = END_COL[[i]])))
# The registered score's label breaks onto two lines so the four labels fit
# under their violins.
END_LAB <- c("Desert theory", "Just deserts", "Just deserts\n(registered)", "Revenge")
endorse_long$measure <- END_LAB[match(endorse_long$measure, ENDORSE)]
endorse_plot <- endorse; endorse_plot$measure <- END_LAB[match(endorse$measure, ENDORSE)]
f12a <- violins_1to7(endorse_long, endorse_plot, END_LAB) +
  labs(title = "A. Endorsement")
assoc <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(ENDORSE), function(i)
  cbind(measure = ENDORSE[i], cor_ci2(s2p$punit_parts6, END_COL[[i]]))))
# GUARDS: each correlation against 01's export for it, on the six components:
# desert theory and revenge (PAPER_H10_cors, .674 and .676), the paper's just
# deserts (PAPER_JD_H10_cors, .432), and the registered just deserts
# (DS_revenge_darkside's reference row, .468).
h10c <- read_s2("PAPER_H10_cors")
h10f <- h10c[h10c$x == "Punitiveness (six components)" & h10c$sample == "Whole sample", ]
h10j <- read_s2("PAPER_JD_H10_cors")
h10j <- h10j[h10j$x == "Punitiveness (six components)" & h10j$sample == "Whole sample", ]
jd_reg <- rev3[rev3$x == FULL & grepl("^Just deserts \\(registered\\)", rev3$y), ]
stopifnot(sum(h10f$y == "Desert theory") == 1, sum(h10f$y == "Revenge") == 1,
          sum(h10j$y == "Just deserts") == 1, nrow(jd_reg) == 1)
same(assoc$r[1], h10f$r[h10f$y == "Desert theory"], "desert theory x punitiveness")
same(assoc$r[2], h10j$r[h10j$y == "Just deserts"], "just deserts (paper) x punitiveness")
same(assoc$r[3], jd_reg$r, "just deserts (registered) x punitiveness")
same(assoc$r[4], h10f$r[h10f$y == "Revenge"], "revenge x punitiveness")
assoc$family <- ifelse(assoc$measure == "Revenge", "Revenge", "Retribution")
assoc$measure <- factor(assoc$measure, levels = rev(ENDORSE))
f12b <- bars_r(assoc, "measure", "family", fills = c(Retribution = S2_FILL, Revenge = S1_FILL),
               xlim = c(0, 0.8), xbreaks = seq(0, 0.8, 0.2),
               xlab = expression(paste("Correlation with punitiveness (", italic(r), ") and 95% CI"))) +
  theme(legend.position = "none") + labs(title = "B. Correlation with punitiveness")
fig12 <- f12a / f12b + plot_layout(heights = c(1.3, 0.95))
save_fig(fig12, "fig12_study2_desert_revenge", 5.4)
fig12
```

## Figure 13: the second sentence

```{r figure13_second_sentence, fig.width = 5.8, fig.height = 7.4}
# === FIGURE 13: BOTH SENTENCES (A), WHAT PARTICIPANTS DID (B), AND WHAT
# KEEPING THE SENTENCE GOES WITH (C) ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: A, the two sentences as violins; B, the share who
# reduced, kept or raised the sentence, by whether the first was 50 years; C,
# the sentencing ratio's correlation with desert theory, revenge, punitiveness
# (the five attitude components) and the principle. Every plotted number is
# checked against 01's exports (GUARDS below).
# PREREG: A and B are descriptive; C's rows are NOT REGISTERED as scored.
# CONSUMES: s2, s2p (sections 4.0 and 8); read_s2(), same(), mean_ci(),
#           cor_ci2(), violin_sentences(), bars_r().
sc <- read_s2("P2_sentence_change")
same(mean(s2$Sentence2), sc$M1, "mean second sentence"); same(mean(s2$Sentence1), sc$M2, "mean first sentence")
SENT <- c("First sentence", "Second sentence")
f13a_long <- rbind(data.frame(group = SENT[1], years = s2$Sentence1),
                   data.frame(group = SENT[2], years = s2$Sentence2))
f13a_long$group <- factor(f13a_long$group, levels = SENT)
f13a_stats <- rbind(cbind(group = SENT[1], mean_ci(s2$Sentence1)),
                    cbind(group = SENT[2], mean_ci(s2$Sentence2)))
f13a_stats$group <- factor(f13a_stats$group, levels = SENT)
f13a <- violin_sentences(f13a_long, f13a_stats) + labs(title = "A. Both sentences")
# B: reduced / kept / raised, by whether the first sentence was the maximum.
ok <- s2$Sentence1 > 0
dirn <- ifelse(s2$Sentence2 < s2$Sentence1, "Reduced",
        ifelse(s2$Sentence2 == s2$Sentence1, "Kept", "Raised"))[ok]
GRP <- c("First sentence 50 years (n = 360)", "First sentence under 50 years (n = 587)")
grp <- ifelse(s2$Sentence1[ok] == 50, GRP[1], GRP[2])
tab <- table(factor(grp, levels = GRP), factor(dirn, levels = c("Reduced", "Kept", "Raised")))
cells <- read_s2("sentencing_ratio_direction_cells"); ce <- read_s2("P2_sentence_ceiling")
same(colSums(tab), cells$n, "reduced / kept / raised counts")
same(tab[1, "Kept"], ce$k[1], "kept at 50"); same(tab[2, ], ce$k[2:4], "below 50")
stopifnot(rowSums(tab)[1] == 360, rowSums(tab)[2] == 587)
b_long <- as.data.frame(tab); names(b_long) <- c("group", "choice", "n")
b_long$pct <- 100 * b_long$n / ave(b_long$n, b_long$group, FUN = sum)
b_long$group <- factor(b_long$group, levels = rev(GRP))
f13b <- ggplot(b_long, aes(x = pct, y = group, fill = choice)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.5,
           position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  geom_text(data = b_long[b_long$pct >= 4, ],
            aes(label = sprintf("%.0f%%", pct), group = choice, colour = choice != "Reduced"),
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5, reverse = TRUE), size = 2.6,
            show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = INK), guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Reduced = "#b0b0b0", Kept = "#666666", Raised = "#1a1a1a")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.01))) +
  labs(x = "Participants", y = NULL, title = "B. The second sentence against the first") +
  theme_hbar()
# C: the sentencing ratio with desert theory, revenge (four items, as
# registered), punitiveness and the principle, from s2p. Punitiveness here is
# the five attitude components, each standardized (punit_parts5z), because the
# ratio is built from the sentences and the six-component score contains the
# first sentence. Each r and its interval are checked against PAPER_ratio_cors,
# and revenge and punitiveness also against the paper's continuous analysis of
# the ratio (PAPER_ratio_continuous; its revenge row is 9.10's registered one),
# whose standardized slope equals r. NOT REGISTERED as scored (desert theory,
# the five components).
MEAS13 <- c(desert_theory = "Desert theory", revenge = "Revenge",
            punit_parts5z = "Punitiveness (five attitude components)",
            proportionality_principle = "Proportionality principle")
MEAS13_EXPORT <- c(desert_theory = "Desert theory", revenge = "Revenge",
                   punit_parts5z = "Punitiveness (five attitude components)",
                   proportionality_principle = "Proportionality principle")
rat <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(MEAS13), function(v)
  cbind(measure = MEAS13[[v]], cor_ci2(s2p$sentence_ratio, s2p[[v]]))))
prc <- read_s2("PAPER_ratio_cors"); pcc <- read_s2("PAPER_ratio_continuous")
for (i in seq_along(MEAS13)) {
  e <- prc[prc$y == MEAS13_EXPORT[[i]], ]
  stopifnot(nrow(e) == 1)
  same(c(rat$r[i], rat$lower[i], rat$upper[i]), c(e$r, e$ci_lower, e$ci_upper),
       paste("ratio x", MEAS13[[i]]))
}
# GUARD: the continuous analysis has exactly one punitiveness row, the five
# components (01 guards that no six-component row reads the ratio).
stopifnot(sum(pcc$outcome == "Revenge") == 1, sum(grepl("^Punitiveness", pcc$outcome)) == 1,
          pcc$outcome[grepl("^Punitiveness", pcc$outcome)] == MEAS13_EXPORT[["punit_parts5z"]])
same(rat$r[2], pcc$beta[pcc$outcome == "Revenge"], "ratio x revenge (slope)", tol = 1e-6)
same(rat$r[3], pcc$beta[grepl("^Punitiveness", pcc$outcome)], "ratio x punitiveness (slope)", tol = 1e-6)
rat$measure <- factor(rat$measure, levels = rev(unname(MEAS13)))
rat$shade <- ifelse(rat$measure == "Proportionality principle", "light", "dark")
f13c <- bars_r(rat, "measure", "shade", fills = c(dark = S2_FILL, light = S1_FILL),
               xlim = c(-0.1, 0.42), xbreaks = seq(-0.1, 0.4, 0.1),
               xlab = expression(paste("Correlation with the sentencing ratio (", italic(r), ") and 95% CI"))) +
  theme(legend.position = "none") + labs(title = "C. What keeping the sentence goes with")
fig13 <- f13a / f13b / f13c + plot_layout(heights = c(1.6, 0.8, 0.9))
save_fig(fig13, "fig13_study2_second_sentence", 7.4)
fig13
```
