# 9. Study 2's own figures (Results, Part 3)

These three figures show Study 2 alone, for Part 3 of its Results ("The people
who rank retribution first"). They use the grayscale style of the figures above and
the same kind of checks. Where a plotted number is rebuilt from the scored
data, it is compared with the value `01_main_analysis.Rmd` exported, and the
knit stops if any disagrees. Figure 14B's intervals for the two means have no
exported counterpart and are computed here, and Figure 15's intervals and its
second comparison group's means are read from the exports.

```{r study2_part3_inputs}
# === INPUTS FOR THE PART 3 FIGURES ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: confirms that the exports these figures read exist, and
# fixes the primary grouping from the scored data.
#
# The P3_ files are written by section 9.17 of 01_main_analysis.Rmd. If any is
# missing, 01 has not been knitted since that section was added; knit it first.
P3_NEEDED <- c("P3_grouping_agreement", "P3_sentence_direction_by_ranking",
               "P3_H12_everyone_else", "H12_retributivist_endorsement",
               "retributivist_measure_contrasts", "contrasts_ranking",
               "contrasts_vs_deter_incap")
P3_MISSING <- P3_NEEDED[!file.exists(file.path(S2_TABLES, paste0(P3_NEEDED, ".csv")))]
if (length(P3_MISSING)) stop("Knit 01_main_analysis.Rmd first (the P3_ files come from ",
                             "section 9.17, the others from 5.5, 9.2, 9.3 and 9.12b). ",
                             "Missing: ", paste(P3_MISSING, collapse = ", "))
# The primary grouping exactly as 01 froze it in the scored data: the 371
# participants who ranked "Criminals deserve to be punished" first, against the
# other 577.
RET <- s2$grp_rank == "Retributivist"
stopifnot(!anyNA(RET), sum(RET) == 371, sum(!RET) == 577)
RANK_LAB <- c("Ranked retribution first\n(n = 371)", "Ranked another goal first\n(n = 577)")
```

## Figure 14: how far the groupings agree

```{r figure14_groupings, fig.width = 5.8, fig.height = 6.6}
# === FIGURE 14: AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE GROUPINGS (A), RELATIVE RETRIBUTION BY
# RANKING GROUP (B), AND WHAT EACH RANKING GROUP DID WITH THE SENTENCE (C) ===
# A: for each pair of the three groupings that classify (nearly) the whole
# sample (the ratio has no value for one participant), the
# share of participants the two place on the same side, beside the share
# expected by chance given how many each places on its retributive side. Both
# are rebuilt from the grouping factors 01 froze in the scored data and checked
# against P3_grouping_agreement, together with kappa, which the panel prints
# under each pair's name. (The thirds are left out of the panel: they classify
# only two thirds of the sample. Table 14 gives their agreement.)
side <- data.frame(ranking = as.integer(s2$grp_rank == "Retributivist"),
                   median  = as.integer(s2$grp_med == "High rel. retribution"),
                   ratio   = as.integer(s2$grp_ratio == "High sentencing ratio"))
agr <- read_s2("P3_grouping_agreement")
# The export's first three rows are these three pairs, in this order.
stopifnot(grepl("^Ranking", agr$first[1]), grepl("^Median", agr$second[1]),
          grepl("^Ranking", agr$first[2]), grepl("^Sentencing", agr$second[2]),
          grepl("^Median", agr$first[3]), grepl("^Sentencing", agr$second[3]))
PAIRS <- list(c("ranking", "median", "Ranking and median split"),
              c("ranking", "ratio",  "Ranking and sentencing ratio"),
              c("median",  "ratio",  "Median split and sentencing ratio"))
f14a_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(PAIRS), function(i) {
  pr <- PAIRS[[i]]
  ok <- !is.na(side[[pr[1]]]) & !is.na(side[[pr[2]]])
  x <- side[[pr[1]]][ok]; y <- side[[pr[2]]][ok]
  po <- mean(x == y)
  pe <- mean(x) * mean(y) + (1 - mean(x)) * (1 - mean(y))
  kap <- (po - pe) / (1 - pe)
  same(po, agr$agreement[i], paste("agreement,", pr[3]))
  same(pe, agr$chance_agreement[i], paste("chance agreement,", pr[3]))
  same(kap, agr$kappa[i], paste("kappa,", pr[3]))
  data.frame(pair = sprintf("%s\n(κ = %s)", pr[3], fmt_r(kap)),
             kind = c("Classified the same way", "Expected by chance"),
             pct = 100 * c(po, pe))
}))
f14a_df$pair <- factor(f14a_df$pair, levels = rev(unique(f14a_df$pair)))
# position_dodge() puts the first level lowest in each row, so the levels are
# reversed to put the observed bar on top.
f14a_df$kind <- factor(f14a_df$kind, levels = c("Expected by chance", "Classified the same way"))
# The 50% line is drawn first, under the bars and labels, and each label sits
# on a white ground (group = kind keeps each label with its own bar).
f14a <- ggplot(f14a_df, aes(x = pct, y = pair, fill = kind)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 50, linetype = "dashed", colour = INK2, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_col(width = 0.75, position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  # pmax() starts every label past the 50% line, so none touches it.
  geom_label(aes(x = pmax(pct, 50) + 1.2, label = sprintf("%.1f%%", pct), group = kind),
             hjust = 0, size = 2.6, colour = INK, fill = "white", linewidth = 0,
             label.padding = unit(0.06, "lines"), position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`Classified the same way` = S2_FILL,
                               `Expected by chance` = S1_FILL),
                    breaks = c("Classified the same way", "Expected by chance")) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), breaks = seq(0, 100, 25),
                     labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
  labs(x = "Participants", y = NULL, title = "A. Agreement between the groupings") +
  theme_hbar()

# B: relative retribution by ranking group. Relative retribution is the
# retribution mean minus the mean of the other three goals, so 0 (the dashed
# line) means retribution rated level with the average of the others. The two
# means are checked against retributivist_measure_contrasts; the 95% intervals
# are t intervals computed here (that export has no interval for a mean).
mc <- read_s2("retributivist_measure_contrasts")
mc_rel <- mc[mc$outcome == "Relative retribution", ]
same(mean(s2$retribution_rel[RET]), mc_rel$M1, "relative retribution, retributivists")
same(mean(s2$retribution_rel[!RET]), mc_rel$M2, "relative retribution, others")
f14b_long <- data.frame(group = ifelse(RET, RANK_LAB[1], RANK_LAB[2]),
                        score = s2$retribution_rel)
f14b_long$group <- factor(f14b_long$group, levels = RANK_LAB)
f14b_stats <- rbind(cbind(group = RANK_LAB[1], mean_ci(s2$retribution_rel[RET])),
                    cbind(group = RANK_LAB[2], mean_ci(s2$retribution_rel[!RET])))
f14b_stats$group <- factor(f14b_stats$group, levels = RANK_LAB)
f14b <- ggplot(f14b_long, aes(x = group, y = score)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = INK2, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_violin(fill = VIOLIN, colour = "#7a7a7a", linewidth = 0.35, width = 0.85,
              adjust = 1.2, trim = TRUE) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.2, height = 0, seed = 1),
             size = 0.6, alpha = 0.35, colour = POINTS, stroke = 0) +
  geom_errorbar(data = f14b_stats, aes(x = group, ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
                inherit.aes = FALSE, width = 0.12, linewidth = 0.6, colour = INK) +
  geom_point(data = f14b_stats, aes(x = group, y = mean), inherit.aes = FALSE,
             size = 2.2, colour = INK) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = -3:3, labels = function(x) sub("^-", "−", x)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Relative retribution",
       title = "B. Relative retribution by ranking group") +
  theme_vbar()

# C: reduced, kept, or raised the second sentence, by ranking group, for the 947
# participants with a sentencing ratio. Counts are checked against
# P3_sentence_direction_by_ranking.
okr <- !is.na(s2$sentence_ratio)
dir14 <- ifelse(s2$sentence_ratio < 1, "Reduced",
                ifelse(s2$sentence_ratio == 1, "Kept", "Raised"))[okr]
grp14 <- ifelse(RET[okr], RANK_LAB[1], RANK_LAB[2])
tab14 <- table(factor(grp14, levels = RANK_LAB),
               factor(dir14, levels = c("Reduced", "Kept", "Raised")))
pd <- read_s2("P3_sentence_direction_by_ranking")
stopifnot(pd$group[1] == "Retributivist", pd$group[2] == "Other")
same(tab14[1, ], unlist(pd[1, c("reduced", "kept", "raised")]), "directions, retributivists")
same(tab14[2, ], unlist(pd[2, c("reduced", "kept", "raised")]), "directions, others")
# Panel C rests on the 947 participants with a ratio, so its row labels carry
# the group sizes of that subset (371 and 576), not of the whole sample.
C_LAB <- sprintf(c("Ranked retribution first\n(n = %d)", "Ranked another goal first\n(n = %d)"),
                 as.integer(rowSums(tab14)))
c_long <- as.data.frame(tab14); names(c_long) <- c("group", "choice", "n")
c_long$pct <- 100 * c_long$n / ave(c_long$n, c_long$group, FUN = sum)
c_long$group <- factor(C_LAB[match(as.character(c_long$group), RANK_LAB)], levels = rev(C_LAB))
f14c <- ggplot(c_long, aes(x = pct, y = group, fill = choice)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.5,
           position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  # Segments narrower than 6% are left unlabelled; the label would not fit.
  geom_text(data = c_long[c_long$pct >= 6, ],
            aes(label = sprintf("%.0f%%", pct), group = choice,
                colour = choice != "Reduced"),
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5, reverse = TRUE), size = 2.6,
            show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = INK), guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Reduced = "#b0b0b0", Kept = "#666666", Raised = "#1a1a1a")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.01))) +
  labs(x = "Participants", y = NULL, title = "C. The second sentence against the first") +
  theme_hbar()
fig14 <- f14a / f14b / f14c + plot_layout(heights = c(1, 1.5, 0.6))
save_fig(fig14, "fig14_study2_groupings", 6.6)
fig14
```

## Figure 15: retributivists against the participants who ranked deterrence or incapacitation first

```{r figure15_contrasts, fig.width = 5.8, fig.height = 6.6}
# === FIGURE 15: COHEN'S d FOR EVERY CONTRAST, RETRIBUTIVISTS AGAINST THE
# PARTICIPANTS WHO RANKED DETERRENCE OR INCAPACITATION FIRST (NOT REGISTERED),
# GROUPED AS IN TABLE S19 ===
# CONSUMES: s2p with punit_parts6 (study2_paper_scorings); RET (Part 3 inputs);
#           read_s2(), same().
# The paper's main text reports this comparison, which leaves out the 124 who
# ranked rehabilitation first; the registered comparison with all 577 other
# participants is in Table S19. The d values and intervals are read from 9.19's
# export (PAPER_contrasts_vs_deter_incap, identical to 9.12b's run). Two checks
# tie them to the data: each retributivist mean is rebuilt from the scored
# data, and each d is rebuilt from its own means and SDs (the difference in
# means divided by the square root of the mean of the two variances), the
# standardizer 01 uses. The comparison group's means cannot be rebuilt here,
# because the scored data do not carry the goal each participant ranked first.
# Punitiveness is the six components (H21, once; NOT REGISTERED as scored),
# cognitive reflection the two-item score, and revenge and the cluster are as
# registered; the five-component punitiveness row, the three-item reflection
# score and the shark decision are not plotted, and Table S19 reports them.
# s2p carries the six-component score under the variable name the export uses
# (punit_parts6), so the retributivist-mean check below reads it directly.
cq15 <- read_s2("PAPER_contrasts_vs_deter_incap")
stopifnot(all(cq15$n1 %in% c(369, 371)), all(cq15$n2 %in% c(452, 453)))
ROWS15 <- data.frame(
  outcome = c("Hostile-aggression cluster (z)",
              "Degradation", "Social exclusion",
              "Punitiveness (six components)",
              "Sentence 1 (z within vignette)", "Harsh prison conditions",
              "Infliction of suffering", "Tolerance of prison violence",
              "Due-process permissiveness", "Convicting on uncertain evidence",
              "Revenge", "Hatred", "Anger",
              "Essentialism about criminals", "Crime is a choice",
              "Leaning toward the prosecution", "Rejecting society's responsibility",
              "Perceived crime rates", "Fear of crime", "Shark: how painful the death should be",
              "Right-Wing Authoritarianism", "Social Dominance Orientation",
              "Violence proneness", "Racial resentment",
              "Cognitive reflection (0-2, lily pad dropped)"),
  label = c("Hostile aggression cluster (H13)",
            "Degradation of prisoners (H13)", "Social exclusion (H13)",
            "Punitiveness (H21)",
            "First sentence (H14)", "Harsh prison conditions (H13)",
            "Infliction of suffering (H13)", "Tolerance of prison violence (H13)",
            "Due-process permissiveness (H20)", "Convicting on uncertain evidence (H20)",
            "Revenge (H13)", "Hatred (H13)", "Anger (H13)",
            "Essentialism (H16)", "Crime is a choice (H17)",
            "Prosecution leaning (H18)", "Rejecting society’s responsibility (H19)",
            "Perceived crime rates (H13)", "Fear of crime (H13)", "Painful death, shark (H15)",
            "Authoritarianism", "Social dominance",
            "Violence proneness", "Racial resentment", "Cognitive reflection"),
  # The same blocks, in the same order, as Table 15's subheadings, less its
  # shark-decision block (an odds ratio, not a d).
  block = rep(c("Summary\nof H13", "Dignity", "Leniency", "Hard\ntreatment", "Certainty\nof guilt",
                "Transcending\nrevenge", "Beliefs about\noffenders\nand trials",
                "Crime\nconcerns and\nthe shark", "Exploratory\n(E1)"),
              times = c(1, 2, 3, 2, 2, 3, 4, 3, 5)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
stopifnot(all(ROWS15$outcome %in% cq15$outcome), nrow(ROWS15) == 25)
d_from <- function(r) (r$M1 - r$M2) / sqrt((r$SD1^2 + r$SD2^2) / 2)
for (o in ROWS15$outcome) {
  b <- cq15[cq15$outcome == o, ]
  y <- s2p[[b$variable]]
  same(mean(y[RET], na.rm = TRUE), b$M1, paste("retributivist mean,", o))
  same(d_from(b), b$d, paste("d against deterrence or incapacitation first,", o), tol = 1e-6)
}
f15_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(ROWS15)), function(i) {
  b <- cq15[cq15$outcome == ROWS15$outcome[i], ]
  data.frame(label = ROWS15$label[i], block = ROWS15$block[i],
             d = b$d, lower = b$d_lower, upper = b$d_upper)
}))
f15_df$label <- factor(f15_df$label, levels = rev(ROWS15$label))
f15_df$block <- factor(f15_df$block, levels = unique(ROWS15$block))
fig15 <- ggplot(f15_df, aes(x = d, y = label)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.62, fill = S2_FILL) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper), width = 0.3, orientation = "y",
                linewidth = 0.3, colour = INK) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = INK2, linewidth = 0.4) +
  facet_grid(block ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-0.2, 1, 0.2),
                     labels = function(x) sub("^-", "−", sprintf("%.1f", x))) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-0.2, 1.0)) +
  labs(x = expression(paste("Retributivists minus deterrence- or incapacitation-first (Cohen’s ",
                            italic(d), ") and 95% CI")), y = NULL) +
  theme_hbar() +
  theme(strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0, size = 7.5, colour = INK2),
        panel.spacing.y = unit(0.35, "lines"))
save_fig(fig15, "fig15_study2_retributivist_contrasts", 6.6)
fig15
```

## Figure 16: endorsement of the hostile attitudes

```{r figure16_endorsement, fig.width = 5.8, fig.height = 4.0}
# === FIGURE 16: SHARE ENDORSING EACH HOSTILE ATTITUDE, RETRIBUTIVISTS (H12)
# AND THE PARTICIPANTS WHO RANKED DETERRENCE OR INCAPACITATION FIRST (NOT
# REGISTERED) ===
# Endorsing means a mean above 4, the scale midpoint; the shark decision is the
# share answering yes. The comparison group is the paper's: the 453 who ranked
# deterrence or incapacitation first, leaving out those who ranked
# rehabilitation first. The retributivists' shares and exact (Clopper-Pearson)
# 95% intervals are rebuilt from the scored data and checked against the H12
# export. The comparison group's are read from 01's export
# (PAPER_H12_shares_vs_deter_incap, section 9.19D), because the scored data do
# not record which goal each participant ranked first.
h12x <- read_s2("H12_retributivist_endorsement"); dix <- read_s2("PAPER_H12_shares_vs_deter_incap")
VAR12 <- data.frame(
  var = c("hatred", "suffering", "degradation", "harsh", "dueprocess", "prisonviol",
          "uncertain", "Shark_3", "shark_kill"),
  export = c("Hatred toward offenders", "Infliction of suffering", "Degradation of prisoners",
             "Harsh prison conditions", "Restricting due-process rights",
             "Tolerance of prison violence", "Convicting on substandard evidence",
             "A painful death for the shark", "Putting the shark to death (yes)"),
  label = c("Hatred", "Infliction of suffering", "Degradation of prisoners",
            "Harsh prison conditions", "Due-process permissiveness",
            "Tolerance of prison violence", "Convicting on uncertain evidence",
            "Painful death for the shark", "Would put the shark to death"),
  block = c(rep("Attitudes H12 lists", 8), "Added in\nthe analysis"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
share_ci <- function(x) {
  k <- sum(x); n <- length(x); bt <- binom.test(k, n)
  data.frame(pct = 100 * k / n, lower = 100 * bt$conf.int[1], upper = 100 * bt$conf.int[2])
}
GRP16 <- c("Ranked retribution first (n = 371)",
           "Ranked deterrence or incapacitation first (n = 453; not registered)")
f16_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(VAR12)), function(i) {
  v <- VAR12$var[i]
  endorse <- if (v == "shark_kill") s2[[v]] == 1 else s2[[v]] > 4
  stopifnot(!anyNA(endorse))
  a <- share_ci(endorse[RET])
  ea <- h12x[h12x$attitude == VAR12$export[i], ]; eb <- dix[dix$attitude == VAR12$export[i], ]
  stopifnot(nrow(ea) == 1, nrow(eb) == 1, eb$n == 453)
  same(a$pct / 100, ea$share, paste("retributivist share,", v))
  same(a$lower / 100, ea$share_ci_lower, paste("retributivist lower limit,", v))
  same(a$upper / 100, ea$share_ci_upper, paste("retributivist upper limit,", v))
  b <- data.frame(pct = 100 * eb$share, lower = 100 * eb$share_ci_lower,
                  upper = 100 * eb$share_ci_upper)
  same(eb$share, eb$k_endorsing / eb$n, paste("comparison share is k / n,", v))
  cbind(label = VAR12$label[i], block = VAR12$block[i], group = GRP16, rbind(a, b))
}))
f16_df$label <- factor(f16_df$label, levels = rev(VAR12$label))
f16_df$block <- factor(f16_df$block, levels = unique(VAR12$block))
f16_df$group <- factor(f16_df$group, levels = rev(GRP16))
fig16 <- ggplot(f16_df, aes(x = pct, y = label, fill = group)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.78, position = position_dodge(width = 0.82)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper), width = 0.3, orientation = "y",
                linewidth = 0.3, colour = INK, position = position_dodge(width = 0.82)) +
  # The 50% line is drawn before the labels, and each label sits on a white
  # ground.
  geom_vline(xintercept = 50, linetype = "dashed", colour = INK2, linewidth = 0.4) +
  # group = group keeps each label with its own bar: the fixed white fill
  # replaces the fill mapping, which would otherwise carry the grouping.
  # A label that would start just short of the 50% line is moved past it, so no
  # label sits on the line.
  geom_label(aes(x = ifelse(upper + 1.2 > 45 & upper + 1.2 < 50.5, 51.2, upper + 1.2),
                 label = sprintf("%.0f%%", pct), group = group), hjust = 0, size = 2.4,
             colour = INK, fill = "white", linewidth = 0,
             label.padding = unit(0.06, "lines"), position = position_dodge(width = 0.82)) +
  facet_grid(block ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = setNames(c(S2_FILL, S1_FILL), GRP16), breaks = GRP16) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 70), breaks = seq(0, 70, 10),
                     labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Participants endorsing, with 95% CI", y = NULL) +
  theme_hbar() +
  theme(strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0, size = 7.5, colour = INK2))
save_fig(fig16, "fig16_study2_endorsement", 4.0)
fig16
```


# 10. What was written

```{r written}
# === 10. WHAT THIS KNIT WROTE ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: lists the outputs, so the knitted report records what
# it produced.
# GUARD: the paper figures this knit wrote are exactly the seventeen the paper
# uses (fig1, fig2, fig4 to fig18; fig3 is no longer a paper figure), each once,
# and each is now in the manuscript's and the Overleaf figure folders.
PAPER_FIGS_EXPECTED <- c("fig1_study1_sentences", "fig2_study1_cluster_matrix",
                         "fig4_study1_construct_matrix", "fig5_sentences_both_studies",
                         "fig6_correlates_both_studies",
                         "fig7_hostility_advantage_both_studies", "fig17_study2_sentences",
                         "fig18_study2_correlates", "fig8_study2_goals",
                         "fig9_study2_proportionality", "fig10_study2_desert_direction",
                         "fig11_study2_goals_limits", "fig12_study2_desert_revenge",
                         "fig13_study2_second_sentence", "fig14_study2_groupings",
                         "fig15_study2_retributivist_contrasts", "fig16_study2_endorsement")
stopifnot(setequal(PAPER_FIGS, PAPER_FIGS_EXPECTED), !anyDuplicated(PAPER_FIGS),
          all(file.exists(file.path(DOCS_PAPER, paste0(PAPER_FIGS, ".png")))),
          all(file.exists(file.path(OVERLEAF_FIG, paste0(PAPER_FIGS, ".pdf")))))
cat("Paper figures written this knit (PNG to figures/paper, PDF to Overleaf):\n")
print(PAPER_FIGS)
# A copy of fig3 left in the manuscript's folders by an earlier knit is not
# this knit's output; it is named here so it is not mistaken for a current one.
stale <- c(file.path(DOCS_PAPER, "fig3_study1_sensitivity.png"),
           file.path(OVERLEAF_FIG, "fig3_study1_sensitivity.pdf"))
if (any(file.exists(stale)))
  cat("Left from an earlier knit, NOT a current paper figure:",
      paste(basename(stale[file.exists(stale)]), collapse = ", "), "\n")
print(list.files(OUT_FIGURES))
print(list.files(DOCS_PAPER))
print(list.files(OVERLEAF_FIG))
print(list.files(OUT_TABLES, pattern = "^two_study_"))
print(list.files(OUT_TABLES, pattern = "^S1P_"))
```
